AI Valuation-Off: OpenAI vs Anthropic¶

A side-by-side, top-down valuation model for two pre-IPO AI companies, built as a learning project.

0. Summary¶

▶ Show code
# Summary: the text is built from the model's outputs at the end of Section 10 (summary_text()), so no number is typed.
# This cell shows a placeholder; Section 10's setup cell replaces it in place (display_id "summary").
from IPython.display import Markdown, display

_summary = display(Markdown("*The summary fills in when the notebook has run to the end (Section 10).*"), display_id="summary")

I valued OpenAI and Anthropic with the same top-down model: reported revenue, four possible futures, ten years of cash, then today's value weighted by how likely I think each future is.

The answer. Anthropic wins the valuation-off, but only as the less expensive of two companies priced above my value. My weighted value is $849B against its last round of $965B (0.88), and $483B for OpenAI against $852B (0.57).

The three numbers that matter most

  1. Discount rate: I use 14% until the IPO, falling to 10% by 2030. What would change the answer most: the public-company rate. The prices need about 7%–9% instead of my 10%, with the 4% pre-IPO premium on top until the IPO (Section 9).
  2. Base 2030 operating margin: 15% (OpenAI) and 20% (Anthropic). Each $1 reinvested then earns 35.5% / 47.4% a year, against my 10% rate after the IPO, so this decides whether growth adds value.
  3. Bull value: $1,934B / $2,323B. Against the prices, every price sits inside the range of my futures (price ÷ Bull value 0.4–0.9x), so a future I modelled can explain each one; the gap is in the odds I give it.

Biggest uncertainty. How fast losses turn into profit: my margins start from the companies' own 2026 figures (-83% / -33%, cash burn used as a stand-in, grade C) and rise in a straight line to 2030. They rest on plans shown to investors and leaked figures, not audited accounts.

My judgement. The scenario probabilities (Bull 20% / 25%, Bust 15% / 10%) are my judgement, not sourced facts. A future cannot count below zero (limited liability). Values are enterprise values; cash is not added.

Draft – to be rewritten in my own words.

What is a "valuation-off"?¶

A valuation-off values two similar companies side by side, with the same methods and the same scrutiny, so differences in the result come from the businesses, not from how generously each was modelled. OpenAI and Anthropic are both pre-IPO and neither has public audited accounts, so this model is built top-down from reported figures.

How every number is graded

  • A: the company itself (blog, press release, on-record executive).
  • B: a major outlet (FT, Reuters, Bloomberg, WSJ, CNBC, The Information, Axios, NYT). A leaked draft S-1 reported by them is B.
  • C: blogs, aggregators, competitors' claims about rivals, my own assumptions. Used only as labelled sensitivities.

A number is graded by its original source. Missing numbers stay GAPs, never guesses.

import base64
import html
import io

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from IPython.display import HTML, Markdown, display
from pathlib import Path

DATA_DIR = Path("data")
COMPANIES = ["OpenAI", "Anthropic"]

pd.set_option("display.max_colwidth", 80)
plt.rcParams["figure.dpi"] = 110

# Light styling for show_table. Colours are semi-transparent greys so they read on light and dark themes.
TABLE_CSS = """<style>
.vo-table {margin: 0.5em 0 1em 0; font-family: -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 13px;}
.vo-table summary {cursor: pointer; list-style: none; display: inline-block; font-weight: 600; padding: 5px 12px;
                   border: 1px solid rgba(127,127,127,0.4); border-radius: 6px; background: rgba(127,127,127,0.08);}
.vo-table summary::-webkit-details-marker {display: none;}
.vo-table .vo-arrow {display: inline-block; transition: transform 0.15s;}
.vo-table details[open] .vo-arrow {transform: rotate(90deg);}
.vo-table .vo-note {margin: 8px 0 4px 0; opacity: 0.8; font-size: 12px; max-width: 980px;}
.vo-table table {border-collapse: collapse; margin-top: 6px; width: 100%; max-width: 1100px;}
.vo-table th {text-align: left; padding: 5px 9px; border-bottom: 2px solid rgba(127,127,127,0.5); background: rgba(127,127,127,0.06);}
.vo-table td {text-align: left; padding: 4px 9px; border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(127,127,127,0.2); vertical-align: top; max-width: 520px;}
.vo-table tbody tr:nth-child(even) {background: rgba(127,127,127,0.07);}
</style>"""


# Appendix capture: while a section's setup cell runs, its detail tables and charts are stored here
# (instead of being shown) and displayed later, collapsed, in the Appendix.
APPENDIX = {}
_capture = {"part": None}


def capture_to(part):
    # Start sending show_table / show_figure output to an appendix part ("A1", "A2", ...); None stops capturing.
    _capture["part"] = part
    if part:
        APPENDIX[part] = []


def show_table(df, title, collapsed=True, note=None, index=False, float_format="{:,.4g}".format):
    # Render a DataFrame inside a plain-HTML <details> block: hidden behind a "Show table" button when
    # collapsed, open by default otherwise. Plain HTML works in Jupyter, VS Code and the HTML export.
    if _capture["part"]:
        APPENDIX[_capture["part"]].append(("table", dict(df=df.copy(), title=title, note=note, index=index, float_format=float_format)))
        return
    table_html = df.to_html(index=index, border=0, float_format=float_format, na_rep="", escape=True)
    note_html = f'<div class="vo-note">{html.escape(note)}</div>' if note else ""
    n = len(df)
    summary = f'<span class="vo-arrow">&#9654;</span> Show table: {html.escape(title)} ({n} row{"" if n == 1 else "s"})'
    display(HTML(
        f'{TABLE_CSS}<div class="vo-table tex2jax_ignore mathjax_ignore">'
        f'<details{"" if collapsed else " open"}><summary>{summary}</summary>{note_html}{table_html}</details></div>'
    ))


def pct(x, decimals=1):
    # Format a fraction as a percentage string for display tables.
    return "" if pd.isna(x) else f"{x * 100:,.{decimals}f}%"


def _figure_html(fig, title, collapsed, note=None):
    # A chart as an inline PNG inside the same <details> block style as the tables.
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    fig.savefig(buf, format="png", dpi=110, bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.close(fig)
    img = base64.b64encode(buf.getvalue()).decode()
    note_html = f'<div class="vo-note">{html.escape(note)}</div>' if note else ""
    return (f'{TABLE_CSS}<div class="vo-table tex2jax_ignore mathjax_ignore"><details{"" if collapsed else " open"}>'
            f'<summary><span class="vo-arrow">&#9654;</span> Show chart: {html.escape(title)}</summary>{note_html}'
            f'<img src="data:image/png;base64,{img}" style="max-width:100%; margin-top:6px;"></details></div>')


def show_figure(fig, title, collapsed=False, note=None):
    # Main text: show the chart normally. While capturing, or if collapsed: store/show it inside a <details> block.
    if _capture["part"]:
        APPENDIX[_capture["part"]].append(("figure", dict(html=_figure_html(fig, title, True, note))))
    elif collapsed:
        display(HTML(_figure_html(fig, title, True, note)))
    else:
        plt.show()


def show_appendix(part):
    # Display everything captured for one appendix part, all collapsed, in the order it was computed.
    for kind, item in APPENDIX.get(part, []):
        if kind == "table":
            show_table(**item, collapsed=True)
        else:
            display(HTML(item["html"]))

1. How much money do they make?¶

The question: How much revenue does each company really bring in, and how far can I trust the figure?

▶ Show code
# Setup for Section 1: load, check and organise the revenue data (no output here).
# Detail tables and charts produced here are captured and shown, collapsed, in Appendix A1.
capture_to("A1")

# The only allowed revenue types. Each is kept as its own series and never merged with another.
REVENUE_TYPES = {
    "run_rate": "Run-rate (latest month x 12, point in time)",
    "annual_revenue": "Recognised revenue, full year",
    "half_year_revenue": "Recognised revenue, half year",
    "quarter_revenue": "Recognised revenue, quarter",
    "growth_multiple": "Reported growth multiple (x, year on year)",
    "projection": "Company projection / target",
}
ACTUAL_TYPES = ["run_rate", "annual_revenue", "half_year_revenue", "quarter_revenue"]  # reported figures for past periods
BOOKED_MONTHS = {"annual_revenue": 12, "half_year_revenue": 6, "quarter_revenue": 3}  # months each booked type covers
REVENUE_BASES = ["gross", "net", "unknown"]
UNITS = {t: "x" if t == "growth_multiple" else "USD_billions" for t in REVENUE_TYPES}  # growth multiples are ratios

revenue_raw = pd.read_csv(DATA_DIR / "revenue.csv")

revenue = revenue_raw.merge(
    source_log[["source_id", "company", "source_name", "url", "date_published", "grade"]],
    on=["source_id", "company"],
    how="left",
    validate="many_to_one",
    indicator=True,
)

# --- Hard checks: stop the notebook if the data breaks a rule ---
orphans = revenue[revenue["_merge"] != "both"]
assert orphans.empty, f"Revenue rows with no matching source in source_log:\n{orphans}"
revenue = revenue.drop(columns="_merge")

bad_types = set(revenue["type"]) - set(REVENUE_TYPES)
assert not bad_types, f"Unknown revenue types: {bad_types}"
assert (revenue["unit"] == revenue["type"].map(UNITS)).all(), "Revenue must be in USD_billions (growth multiples in x)"
assert revenue["revenue_basis"].isin(REVENUE_BASES).all(), "revenue_basis must be gross, net or unknown"
assert revenue["grade"].isin(["A", "B", "C"]).all(), "Grades must be A, B or C"
assert revenue["value"].gt(0).all(), "Revenue values must be positive"
assert not revenue.duplicated(["source_id", "company", "type", "period", "value"]).any(), "Duplicate rows"

revenue["period_end"] = pd.to_datetime(revenue["period"], format="%Y-%m") + pd.offsets.MonthEnd(0)
revenue["date_published"] = pd.to_datetime(revenue["date_published"])

period_start = revenue["period_end"] - pd.offsets.MonthBegin(1)
published_too_early = revenue["type"].isin(ACTUAL_TYPES + ["growth_multiple"]) & (revenue["date_published"] < period_start)
assert not published_too_early.any(), f"Actuals published before their period:\n{revenue[published_too_early]}"

revenue = revenue.sort_values(["company", "type", "period_end"]).reset_index(drop=True)

rows_by_type = pd.crosstab(revenue["company"], revenue["type"], margins=True, margins_name="Total")
rows_by_type.columns.name = None
show_table(rows_by_type.reset_index().rename(columns={"company": "Company"}), "Revenue rows by company and type",
           collapsed=False,
           note=f"All hard checks passed: {len(revenue)} revenue rows from {revenue['source_id'].nunique()} sources.")


# Outlets CLAUDE.md names as grade B. Any other B-graded outlet is flagged for review.
B_LIST_OUTLETS = ["Financial Times", "Reuters", "Bloomberg", "WSJ", "Wall Street Journal",
                  "CNBC", "The Information", "Axios", "New York Times"]
# Known relays: they rewrite or link other outlets' reporting, so the original must be cited instead.
RELAY_OUTLETS = ["Techmeme", "PYMNTS", "VentureBeat", "TechCrunch", "Fortune", "Yahoo"]


def audit_source_grade(row):
    # Return the reasons a source's grade needs review ('' if none).
    name = row["source_name"]
    issues = []
    if row["grade"] == "A" and row["company"].lower() not in name.lower():
        issues.append("Graded A but cited through a third party; link the company's own statement")
    if row["grade"] == "B":
        if "via" in name.lower() or any(r.lower() in name.lower() for r in RELAY_OUTLETS):
            issues.append("Relay; cite the original article or statement")
        elif not any(name.startswith(outlet) for outlet in B_LIST_OUTLETS):
            issues.append("Outlet not on the CLAUDE.md B list; confirm B or regrade to C")
    if row["grade"] == "C":
        issues.append("C-grade; excluded from model inputs")
    return "; ".join(issues)


source_log["grade_review"] = source_log.apply(audit_source_grade, axis=1)

# Row-level flags: issues visible only in the source text (judgement calls, each with its reason).
ROW_FLAGS = {  # keyed by (source_id, type, period)
    ("OA1", "run_rate", "2023-11"): "Retrospective figure cited as a prior data point; original report not verified",
    ("OA3", "run_rate", "2024-12"): "Possible conflict: OpenAI's CFO post (OA6) reportedly gives about $6B annualized revenue for 2024",
    ("OA9", "quarter_revenue", "2026-03"): "Approximate: source says 'about $5.7 billion'",
    ("AN3", "run_rate", "2026-03"): "Lower bound: body says 'surpassed $19B' (headline: 'nears $20B')",
    ("AN11", "annual_revenue", "2025-12"): "Approximate: 'nearly $4.6B'. Leaked draft S-1 via Reuters, not a public filing",
    ("AN11", "growth_multiple", "2025-12"): "Approximate: 'twelvefold'. Used only to derive FY2024",
    ("AN13", "quarter_revenue", "2026-06"): "Leaked draft S-1 via the FT, not a public filing",
}
revenue["row_flag"] = [ROW_FLAGS.get(k, "") for k in zip(revenue["source_id"], revenue["type"], revenue["period"])]
revenue = revenue.merge(source_log[["source_id", "grade_review"]], on="source_id", how="left")
revenue["review"] = (revenue["grade_review"] + "; " + revenue["row_flag"]).str.strip("; ")

# The set later sections use: C-grade rows excluded.
revenue_model = revenue[revenue["grade"] != "C"].copy()

used = source_log[source_log["source_id"].isin(revenue["source_id"])]
n_flagged = (used["grade_review"] != "").sum()
show_table(
    used[["source_id", "company", "source_name", "grade"]].assign(audit=used["grade_review"].replace("", "OK")),
    "Grade audit: sources used in Section 1",
    note=f"{n_flagged} of {len(used)} sources flagged. {len(revenue) - len(revenue_model)} revenue rows excluded as C-grade.",
)
show_table(
    revenue.loc[revenue["row_flag"] != "", ["source_id", "company", "type", "period", "value", "unit", "row_flag"]],
    "Row-level flags", collapsed=False,
    note="Flagged rows stay in the model; the flag travels with them into later sections.",
)


s1_corrections = pd.read_csv(DATA_DIR / "s1_corrections.csv")
show_table(s1_corrections, "Section 1 corrections log",
           note="Includes one requested change that was reviewed and not applied (item 11, AN3), with the reason.")


def show_revenue_table(company, rev=revenue_model):
    # One collapsed table per company: every figure, grouped by revenue type.
    d = rev[rev["company"] == company].copy()
    d["type_order"] = d["type"].map({t: i for i, t in enumerate(REVENUE_TYPES)})
    d = d.sort_values(["type_order", "period_end"])
    out = pd.DataFrame({
        "type": d["type"].map(REVENUE_TYPES),
        "period": d["period"],
        "value": d["value"],
        "unit": d["unit"],
        "basis": d["revenue_basis"],
        "grade": d["grade"],
        "source": d["source_id"] + " " + d["source_name"],
        "published": d["date_published"].dt.date,
        "review": d["review"],
    })
    show_table(out, f"{company}: all revenue figures",
               note="Run-rates, booked revenue and projections are different measures and are never combined into one series.")


for company in COMPANIES:
    show_revenue_table(company)


AS_OF = pd.Timestamp("2026-10-02")  # date the dataset was last updated (not a financial input)

# Figures we would want for each company: (description, type, period)
GAP_CHECKS = [
    ("FY2024 recognised revenue", "annual_revenue", "2024-12"),
    ("FY2025 recognised revenue", "annual_revenue", "2025-12"),
    ("H1 2025 recognised revenue", "half_year_revenue", "2025-06"),
    ("H1 2026 recognised revenue", "half_year_revenue", "2026-06"),
    ("Q1 2026 recognised revenue", "quarter_revenue", "2026-03"),
    ("Q2 2026 recognised revenue", "quarter_revenue", "2026-06"),
    ("Exit run-rate, Dec 2024", "run_rate", "2024-12"),
    ("Exit run-rate, Dec 2025", "run_rate", "2025-12"),
]


def derived_prior_year_revenue(company, year, rev=revenue_model):
    # FY(year) DERIVED as FY(year + 1) booked revenue / reported growth multiple. None if either input is missing.
    d = rev[rev["company"] == company]
    nxt = d[(d["type"] == "annual_revenue") & (d["period"] == f"{year + 1}-12")]
    mult = d[(d["type"] == "growth_multiple") & (d["period"] == f"{year + 1}-12")]
    if nxt.empty or mult.empty:
        return None
    n, m = nxt.iloc[0], mult.iloc[0]
    return {"company": company, "item": f"FY{year} recognised revenue", "derived_usd_bn": n["value"] / m["value"],
            "how derived": f"FY{year + 1} ${n['value']:g}B ({n['source_id']}) / {m['value']:g}x growth ({m['source_id']})",
            "label": "derived, not reported"}


def gap_register(company, rev=revenue_model):
    rows = []
    d = rev[rev["company"] == company]
    for label, rev_type, period in GAP_CHECKS:
        hit = d[(d["type"] == rev_type) & (d["period"] == period)]
        status = "GAP" if hit.empty else "; ".join(
            f"${v:g}B ({s}, grade {g})" for v, s, g in zip(hit["value"], hit["source_id"], hit["grade"]))
        derived = derived_prior_year_revenue(company, int(period[:4])) if hit.empty and rev_type == "annual_revenue" else None
        if derived:
            status += f" (derived, not reported: ${derived['derived_usd_bn']:.2f}B)"
        rows.append({"item": label, "company": company, "status": status})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


gaps = pd.concat([gap_register(c) for c in COMPANIES])
gap_table = gaps.pivot(index="item", columns="company", values="status").loc[[g[0] for g in GAP_CHECKS], COMPANIES]
gap_table.columns.name = None
show_table(gap_table.reset_index(), "Gap register", collapsed=False,
           note="GAP = no A- or B-grade figure found. A derived figure is shown next to a gap but never closes it.")

s1_derived = pd.DataFrame([x for c in COMPANIES for y in [2024] if (x := derived_prior_year_revenue(c, y))])
show_table(s1_derived, "Derived figures (computed from reported inputs, not reported themselves)", collapsed=False,
           note="Grade of a derived figure = the weaker of its inputs (here B). Section 1.8 notes an independent cross-check.")


def key_figures(company, rev=revenue_model):
    # Latest actual of each type for one company.
    d = rev[(rev["company"] == company) & rev["type"].isin(ACTUAL_TYPES)]
    latest = d.sort_values("period_end").groupby("type").tail(1)
    return latest.assign(
        months_old=lambda x: ((AS_OF - x["period_end"]).dt.days / 30.44).round(1)
    )[["company", "type", "period", "value", "revenue_basis", "grade", "source_id", "months_old", "row_flag", "grade_review"]]


s1_key_figures = pd.concat([key_figures(c) for c in COMPANIES]).reset_index(drop=True)
show_table(s1_key_figures.drop(columns="grade_review").rename(columns={"value": "USD bn"}),
           "Key figures: latest reported figure of each type (s1_key_figures)", collapsed=False,
           note=f"months_old is measured from AS_OF = {AS_OF.date()}.")


FIGURE_TYPES = ["reported", "adjusted", "projection", "commitment", "target"]

financials = pd.read_csv(DATA_DIR / "financials.csv").merge(
    source_log[["source_id", "company", "source_name", "date_published", "grade"]].rename(columns={"company": "source_company"}),
    on="source_id", how="left", validate="many_to_one", indicator=True,
)
assert (financials["_merge"] == "both").all(), "financials.csv row with no matching source in source_log"
financials = financials.drop(columns="_merge")
# A source must be about the same company, or about both ('Both').
assert (financials["source_company"].isin(["Both"]) | (financials["source_company"] == financials["company"])).all()
assert financials["unit"].isin(["USD_billions", "percent", "year"]).all(), "financials units: USD_billions, percent or year"
assert financials["figure_type"].isin(FIGURE_TYPES).all(), f"figure_type must be one of {FIGURE_TYPES}"
assert financials["grade"].isin(["A", "B", "C"]).all(), "Grades must be A, B or C"
assert not financials.duplicated(["source_id", "company", "metric", "figure_type", "period"]).any(), "Duplicate financials rows"

show_table(financials[["company", "metric", "figure_type", "period", "value", "unit", "grade", "source_id", "notes"]]
           .sort_values(["company", "metric", "period"]),
           "Non-revenue figures for Section 3 (financials.csv)",
           note=f"{len(financials)} rows. Reported, adjusted, projected, committed and target figures are kept apart by figure_type.")


from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
from matplotlib.ticker import FixedLocator, FuncFormatter

COMPANY_COLOURS = {"OpenAI": "#1f77b4", "Anthropic": "#d95f02"}
GRADE_MARKERS = {"A": "*", "B": "o", "C": "X"}
GRADE_MARKER_SIZES = {"A": 150, "B": 45, "C": 60}
LABEL_OFFSETS = {"OpenAI": (8, -26), "Anthropic": (-10, 10)}  # keep the two latest-value labels apart


def plot_company_revenue(ax, company, rev=revenue_model):
    # Plot one company's run-rate (solid) and projections (dashed, one line per source).
    colour = COMPANY_COLOURS[company]
    d = rev[rev["company"] == company]

    run_rate = d[d["type"] == "run_rate"].sort_values("period_end")
    ax.plot(run_rate["period_end"], run_rate["value"], color=colour, lw=2, ls="-", zorder=2)

    projections = d[d["type"] == "projection"]
    for _, forecast in projections.groupby("source_id"):
        forecast = forecast.sort_values("period_end")
        ax.plot(forecast["period_end"], forecast["value"], color=colour, lw=1.5, ls="--", zorder=2)

    for grade, pts in pd.concat([run_rate, projections]).groupby("grade"):
        ax.scatter(pts["period_end"], pts["value"], marker=GRADE_MARKERS[grade],
                   s=GRADE_MARKER_SIZES[grade], color=colour, edgecolor="white", linewidth=0.6, zorder=3)

    latest = run_rate.iloc[-1]
    ax.annotate(f"${latest['value']:g}B run-rate\n({latest['period_end']:%b %Y})",
                (latest["period_end"], latest["value"]), textcoords="offset points",
                xytext=LABEL_OFFSETS[company], ha="left" if LABEL_OFFSETS[company][0] > 0 else "right",
                fontsize=8.5, color="#333333")


def plot_revenue_chart():
    # Run-rates (solid) and company projections (dashed), log scale.
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5.8))
    for company in COMPANIES:
        plot_company_revenue(ax, company)

    ax.set_yscale("log")
    ax.yaxis.set_major_locator(FixedLocator([0.1, 0.3, 1, 3, 10, 30, 100, 300]))
    ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: f"${v:g}B"))
    ax.yaxis.set_minor_formatter(FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: ""))
    ax.set_ylabel("Revenue (USD billions, log scale)")
    ax.set_xlabel("Period the figure refers to")
    ax.set_title("Reported run-rate vs company projections (not audited)", loc="left", fontsize=12)
    ax.grid(True, which="major", color="#dddddd", lw=0.7)
    ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)

    legend_handles = [
        Line2D([], [], color=COMPANY_COLOURS["OpenAI"], lw=2, label="OpenAI"),
        Line2D([], [], color=COMPANY_COLOURS["Anthropic"], lw=2, label="Anthropic"),
        Line2D([], [], color="#555555", lw=2, ls="-", label="Run-rate (reported actual)"),
        Line2D([], [], color="#555555", lw=1.5, ls="--", label="Company projection, full-year revenue\n(one line per source)"),
    ] + [
        Line2D([], [], color="#555555", marker=GRADE_MARKERS[g], ls="", markersize=ms, label=f"Grade {g} source")
        for g, ms in [("A", 11), ("B", 6), ("C", 7)]
    ]
    ax.legend(handles=legend_handles, loc="lower right", fontsize=8.5, frameon=True, framealpha=0.95, edgecolor="#dddddd")

    fig.text(
        0.01, -0.02,
        "Note on the log scale: each step up the y-axis multiplies revenue (by roughly 3x per gridline) rather than adding a fixed amount.\n"
        "This lets \\$0.09B and \\$350B fit on one chart, and a straight line means a constant percentage growth rate. The catch: large\n"
        "dollar gaps look small, so read gaps between lines as ratios, not dollar differences.",
        fontsize=8.5, color="#444444", va="top",
    )
    plt.tight_layout()
    return fig


def headline_revenue_table():
    # Latest run-rate, latest booked quarter and FY2025 booked revenue for each company, with grade (GAP if missing).
    def cell(company, rev_type, period=None):
        d = revenue_model[(revenue_model["company"] == company) & (revenue_model["type"] == rev_type)]
        if period:
            d = d[d["period"] == period]
        if d.empty:
            return "GAP"
        r = d.sort_values("period_end").iloc[-1]
        return f"${r['value']:g}B ({r['period']}, grade {r['grade']})"
    return pd.DataFrame([{"company": c, "latest run-rate": cell(c, "run_rate"), "latest booked quarter": cell(c, "quarter_revenue"),
                          "FY2025 booked revenue": cell(c, "annual_revenue", "2025-12")} for c in COMPANIES])


capture_to(None)

1.1 What does "revenue" mean?¶

Headlines say "revenue" but mean one of three things, which I never mix:

Term Meaning Watch out for
Run-rate This month's revenue × 12: a snapshot The company picks the month and what counts
Booked revenue Revenue actually earned over a year, half-year or quarter Backward-looking; here from leaks, not audited accounts
Projection What the company expects for a future year A hope, not a result

Gross vs net. Anthropic counts the full price of sales made through Amazon's and Google's clouds and books the partners' cut as a cost (gross). OpenAI counts only its own share of sales through Microsoft (net), so Anthropic's figures look slightly bigger for the same business.

1.2 The numbers¶

The chart shows each company's reported run-rate (solid line) and its own forecasts (dashed). The y-axis is a log scale: each step multiplies rather than adds, so a straight line means steady percentage growth. The table shows the three figures that matter most.

Key Takeaways¶

  • Revenue is often calculated as run-rates, where the revenue of one month is multipled for 12 months.
  • There is a discrepancy between projected run-rates and actual year-end revenue, especially for fast-growing firms.
  • Understanding data sources are crucial which further emphasises the role of grading them.

2. How fast are they growing, and can I trust the numbers?¶

The question: How fast is each company growing, is it slowing down, and are the figures behind it reliable?

▶ Show code
# Setup for Section 2: growth rates, the run-rate test, forecasts and gross vs net (no output here).
# Detail tables and charts produced here are captured and shown, collapsed, in Appendix A2.
capture_to("A2")

def run_rate_series(company, rev=revenue_model):
    # The company's run-rate points (A/B grade only), oldest first.
    d = rev[(rev["company"] == company) & (rev["type"] == "run_rate")].sort_values("period_end")
    assert not d["period"].duplicated().any(), f"{company}: two run-rates for the same month"
    return d[["period", "period_end", "value", "source_id", "grade"]].reset_index(drop=True)


def months_between(start, end):
    return (end.year - start.year) * 12 + (end.month - start.month)


def growth_intervals(company):
    # CMGR, annualised growth and doubling time between each pair of consecutive run-rate points.
    s = run_rate_series(company)
    rows = []
    for prev, curr in zip(s.iloc[:-1].itertuples(), s.iloc[1:].itertuples()):
        months = months_between(prev.period_end, curr.period_end)
        ratio = curr.value / prev.value
        cmgr = ratio ** (1 / months) - 1
        rows.append({
            "company": company,
            "start": prev.period_end, "end": curr.period_end, "months": months,
            "start_usd_bn": prev.value, "end_usd_bn": curr.value,
            "simple_change": ratio - 1,
            "cmgr": cmgr,
            "annualised": (1 + cmgr) ** 12 - 1,
            "doubling_months": np.log(2) / np.log(1 + cmgr),
            "sources": f"{prev.source_id} -> {curr.source_id}",
        })
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


growth = pd.concat([growth_intervals(c) for c in COMPANIES], ignore_index=True)

show_table(
    growth.assign(
        interval=growth["start"].dt.strftime("%b %Y") + " -> " + growth["end"].dt.strftime("%b %Y"),
        simple_change=growth["simple_change"].map(lambda x: pct(x, 0)),
        cmgr=growth["cmgr"].map(pct),
        annualised=growth["annualised"].map(lambda x: pct(x, 0)),
        doubling_months=growth["doubling_months"].round(1),
    )[["company", "interval", "months", "start_usd_bn", "end_usd_bn", "simple_change", "cmgr", "annualised",
       "doubling_months", "sources"]],
    "Growth between consecutive run-rate points",
    note="simple_change depends on the interval length, so it is not comparable across rows; cmgr is. "
         "Growth of the reported run-rate, not of audited revenue.",
)


def plot_interval_cmgr():
    # CMGR between consecutive reported run-rates, one flat segment per interval.
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 4.8))
    for company in COMPANIES:
        g = growth[growth["company"] == company]
        colour = COMPANY_COLOURS[company]
        # Each interval is drawn as a flat segment spanning the months it covers, at its CMGR.
        ax.hlines(g["cmgr"] * 100, g["start"], g["end"], color=colour, lw=2.4)
        mid = g["start"] + (g["end"] - g["start"]) / 2
        ax.scatter(mid, g["cmgr"] * 100, color=colour, s=22, zorder=3)
        for m, y, n in zip(mid, g["cmgr"] * 100, g["months"]):
            ax.annotate(f"{n}m", (m, y), textcoords="offset points", xytext=(0, 6), ha="center", fontsize=7.5, color=colour)

    ax.set_ylabel("CMGR (% per month)")
    ax.set_xlabel("Interval between reported run-rate points")
    ax.set_title("Compounded monthly growth of the reported run-rate, by interval", loc="left", fontsize=12)
    ax.grid(True, color="#dddddd", lw=0.7)
    ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
    ax.legend(handles=[Line2D([], [], color=COMPANY_COLOURS[c], lw=2.4, label=c) for c in COMPANIES],
              loc="upper left", fontsize=9, frameon=False)
    fig.text(0.01, -0.02,
             "Each flat segment spans one interval between two reported run-rates; the label shows its length in months.\n"
             "Short (1-2 month) intervals are noisier: rounding in a headline figure moves their CMGR a lot.",
             fontsize=8.5, color="#444444", va="top")
    plt.tight_layout()
    return fig


show_figure(plot_interval_cmgr(), "Growth by interval: CMGR between consecutive reported run-rates")


def monthly_run_rate_path(company, method="log"):
    # A run-rate for every month from the first to the last reported point.
    # method="log": constant % growth between points; method="linear": constant $ growth between points.
    s = run_rate_series(company)
    known = pd.Series(s["value"].values, index=s["period_end"].dt.to_period("M"))
    months = pd.period_range(known.index.min(), known.index.max(), freq="M")
    x_known = np.array([(p - months[0]).n for p in known.index])
    x_all = np.arange(len(months))
    if method == "log":
        values = np.exp(np.interp(x_all, x_known, np.log(known.values)))
    elif method == "linear":
        values = np.interp(x_all, x_known, known.values)
    else:
        raise ValueError(method)
    return pd.Series(values, index=months, name=f"{company} run-rate ({method})")


def estimate_booked_revenue(company, last_month, n_months, method="log"):
    # Estimated booked revenue for the n_months ending last_month: sum of monthly run-rate / 12.
    # Returns NaN if the window falls outside the reported run-rate path (no extrapolation).
    path = monthly_run_rate_path(company, method)
    window = pd.period_range(end=pd.Period(last_month, freq="M"), periods=n_months, freq="M")
    if not set(window).issubset(path.index):
        return np.nan
    return path.loc[window].sum() / 12


# Step 1: the planned tests, FY2025 for BOTH companies (the only full years with booked revenue for each).
fy25_booked = revenue_model.query("type == 'annual_revenue' and period == '2025-12'").set_index("company")
assert set(COMPANIES) <= set(fy25_booked.index), "Both companies need booked FY2025 revenue for the first test"
first_test = pd.DataFrame([{
    "company": c, "method": m,
    "estimate_usd_bn": estimate_booked_revenue(c, "2025-12", 12, m),
    "reported_usd_bn": fy25_booked.loc[c, "value"],
    "source": f"{fy25_booked.loc[c, 'source_id']} (grade {fy25_booked.loc[c, 'grade']})",
} for c in COMPANIES for m in ["log", "linear"]]).assign(error=lambda d: d["estimate_usd_bn"] / d["reported_usd_bn"] - 1)
show_table(first_test.assign(error=first_test["error"].map(pct)),
           "Bridge test 1: FY2025 estimated from each company's run-rate path vs reported", collapsed=False,
           note="Estimates are estimates (run-rate bridge), not reported. Anthropic's FY2025 is from the leaked draft S-1 (grade B).")


# Step 2: every other booked figure in Section 1 becomes a test case too.
def bridge_tests(rev=revenue_model):
    booked = rev[rev["type"].isin(BOOKED_MONTHS)].sort_values(["company", "period_end"])
    rows = []
    for r in booked.itertuples():
        n = BOOKED_MONTHS[r.type]
        row = {"company": r.company, "period": f"{REVENUE_TYPES[r.type].split(', ')[1]} to {r.period}",
               "reported_usd_bn": r.value, "source": f"{r.source_id} ({r.grade})", "row_flag": r.row_flag}
        for m in ["log", "linear"]:
            est = estimate_booked_revenue(r.company, r.period, n, m)
            row[f"est_{m}"] = est
            row[f"err_{m}"] = est / r.value - 1
        rows.append(row)
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


tests = bridge_tests()
show_table(
    tests.assign(err_log=tests["err_log"].map(pct), err_linear=tests["err_linear"].map(pct))[
        ["company", "period", "reported_usd_bn", "est_log", "err_log", "est_linear", "err_linear", "source", "row_flag"]],
    "Bridge tests: every booked figure we have", collapsed=False,
    note="err = estimate / reported - 1. Negative = the run-rate path under-estimates booked revenue.",
)

bridge_error = pd.DataFrame({
    m: {"mean error": tests[f"err_{m}"].mean(), "mean absolute error": tests[f"err_{m}"].abs().mean(),
        "worst under": tests[f"err_{m}"].min(), "worst over": tests[f"err_{m}"].max(),
        "tests under-estimating": f"{(tests[f'err_{m}'] < 0).sum()} of {len(tests)}"}
    for m in ["log", "linear"]
}).T
error_cols = ["mean error", "mean absolute error", "worst under", "worst over"]
show_table(bridge_error.reset_index(names="method").assign(**{c: bridge_error[c].map(pct).values for c in error_cols}),
           "Bridge error summary", collapsed=False)


# Step 3: only now apply the method where we don't know the answer.
# Error-adjusted range: divide the estimate by (1 + error) for the best and worst log-method test errors.
ERR_MIN, ERR_MAX = tests["err_log"].min(), tests["err_log"].max()
latest_rr = {c: run_rate_series(c).iloc[-1] for c in COMPANIES}


def apply_bridge(company, label, last_month, n_months):
    est = estimate_booked_revenue(company, last_month, n_months, "log")
    return {"company": company, "period": label, "estimate_usd_bn": est,
            "range_low": est / (1 + ERR_MAX), "range_high": est / (1 + ERR_MIN),
            "label": "estimate (log-linear run-rate bridge), not reported"}


bridge_estimates = pd.DataFrame(
    [apply_bridge(c, "H1 2026 (Jan-Jun)", "2026-06", 6) for c in COMPANIES]
    + [apply_bridge(c, f"2026 YTD (Jan-{latest_rr[c]['period_end']:%b})", latest_rr[c]["period"],
                    latest_rr[c]["period_end"].month) for c in COMPANIES]
)
an_2026_quarters = revenue_model.query("company == 'Anthropic' and type == 'quarter_revenue' and period >= '2026-01'")
show_table(bridge_estimates, "Estimated booked revenue from the run-rate path", collapsed=False,
           note="Range = estimate adjusted by the best and worst log-method test errors above. For comparison, "
                f"Anthropic's two reported 2026 quarters sum to ${an_2026_quarters['value'].sum():.2f}B "
                "(a computed sum, not a reported H1 figure; Q2 is a lower bound).")


def projection_check(row, rev=revenue_model):
    # Compare one projection with the actual data most relevant to its target year (rules in the table above).
    company, year = row["company"], row["period_end"].year
    rr = latest_rr[company]
    out = {"company": company, "target": f"FY{year}", "projection_usd_bn": row["value"],
           "made_by": f"{row['source_id']} ({row['grade']}, published {row['date_published']:%b %Y})"}
    booked = rev[(rev["company"] == company) & (rev["type"] == "annual_revenue") & (rev["period_end"].dt.year == year)]
    if year < AS_OF.year:
        if not booked.empty:
            actual, basis = booked.iloc[0]["value"], f"reported booked revenue ({booked.iloc[0]['source_id']})"
        else:
            actual, basis = estimate_booked_revenue(company, f"{year}-12", 12), "estimate (log-linear bridge), not reported"
        gap = actual / row["value"] - 1
        verdict = "Met (within 1%)" if abs(gap) < 0.01 else f"{'Beaten' if gap >= 0 else 'Missed'} by {pct(abs(gap), 0)}"
        if booked.empty and abs(gap) < bridge_error.loc["log", "mean absolute error"]:
            verdict = f"Inconclusive: estimate differs by {pct(gap, 0)}, inside the bridge's average test error"
        out.update(compare_to=actual, compared_with=basis, verdict=verdict)
    elif year == AS_OF.year:
        n_done = rr["period_end"].month
        ytd = estimate_booked_revenue(company, rr["period"], n_done)
        floor = ytd + (12 - n_done) * rr["value"] / 12
        needed = (row["value"] - ytd) * 12 / (12 - n_done)
        out.update(compare_to=ytd, compared_with=f"2026 YTD estimate (Jan-{rr['period_end']:%b}, bridge); "
                                                 f"zero-growth floor ${floor:.1f}B")
        if ytd >= row["value"]:
            out["verdict"] = "Overtaken: estimated revenue booked so far already exceeds the full-year projection"
        elif floor >= row["value"]:
            out["verdict"] = "Consistent even at zero further growth"
        else:
            out["verdict"] = (f"Needs an average run-rate of ${needed:.0f}B for the rest of the year "
                              f"(latest ${rr['value']:g}B, {rr['period_end']:%b %Y}): consistent only if growth continues")
    else:
        out.update(compare_to=rr["value"], compared_with=f"latest run-rate ({rr['period_end']:%b %Y})")
        if rr["value"] >= row["value"]:
            out["verdict"] = "Overtaken: run-rate is already above the target"
        else:
            yrs_mid = (pd.Timestamp(f"{year}-06-30") - rr["period_end"]).days / 365.25
            yrs_end = (pd.Timestamp(f"{year}-12-31") - rr["period_end"]).days / 365.25
            g_mid = (row["value"] / rr["value"]) ** (1 / yrs_mid) - 1
            g_end = (row["value"] / rr["value"]) ** (1 / yrs_end) - 1
            out.update(required_growth_mid=g_mid, required_growth_end=g_end,
                       verdict=f"Needs {pct(g_mid, 0)} a year to mid-{year} ({pct(g_end, 0)} to end-{year})")
    return out

def quarter_vs_run_rate(rev=revenue_model):
    rows = []
    for r in rev[rev["type"] == "quarter_revenue"].sort_values(["company", "period_end"]).itertuples():
        s = run_rate_series(r.company)
        q_end = r.period_end
        q_mid = (q_end - pd.offsets.MonthEnd(1))  # middle month of the quarter
        q_start = q_end - pd.offsets.MonthEnd(2)
        in_q = s[(s["period_end"] >= q_start) & (s["period_end"] <= q_end)]
        nxt = s[s["period_end"] > q_end].head(1)
        x4 = r.value * 4
        row = {"company": r.company, "quarter": f"{q_start:%b}-{q_end:%b %Y}", "quarter revenue x4 (USD bn)": x4,
               "reported run-rates in the quarter": "; ".join(f"${v:g}B ({p:%b})" for v, p in zip(in_q["value"], in_q["period_end"])) or "none"}
        if not nxt.empty:
            n = nxt.iloc[0]
            months = months_between(q_mid, n["period_end"])
            row.update({"next reported run-rate": f"${n['value']:g}B ({n['period_end']:%b %Y})",
                        "next / quarter x4": n["value"] / x4,
                        "monthly growth needed to reconcile": (n["value"] / x4) ** (1 / months) - 1})
        rows.append(row)
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


q_check = quarter_vs_run_rate()

]

oa_same_month = oa_path.loc[an_rr["period_end"].to_period("M")]


def crossover_month(haircut):
    # First month from which haircut-adjusted Anthropic stays above OpenAI to the end of the overlap.
    ahead = an_path.loc[overlap] * (1 - haircut) > oa_path.loc[overlap]
    stays_ahead = ahead[::-1].cummin()[::-1]
    return stays_ahead.idxmax().strftime("%b %Y") if stays_ahead.any() else "no crossover yet"


haircut_table = pd.DataFrame([{
    "haircut": pct(h, 0), "basis for haircut": label, "grade": grade,
    f"Anthropic net-equivalent, {an_rr['period_end']:%b %Y} (USD bn)": an_rr["value"] * (1 - h),
    f"OpenAI {an_rr['period_end']:%b %Y}, interpolated (USD bn)": oa_same_month,
    f"OpenAI {oa_rr['period_end']:%b %Y}, reported (USD bn)": oa_rr["value"],
    "Anthropic still ahead of OpenAI's latest?": "yes" if an_rr["value"] * (1 - h) > oa_rr["value"] else "NO",
    "crossover month (monthly paths)": crossover_month(h),
} for h, label, grade in HAIRCUTS])
show_table(haircut_table, "Gross-vs-net sensitivity: Anthropic's latest run-rate vs OpenAI", collapsed=False,
           note=f"27% = 1 - {claim['value']:g}/{claim_gross['value']:g} (OpenAI's claim vs Anthropic's {claim_gross['period']} "
                "run-rate). Grade C: sensitivity only. Monthly paths are log-linear interpolations (estimates).")


TRAILING_MONTHS = 6


def trailing_growth(company):
    # Trailing 6-month CMGR and year-on-year growth along the interpolated monthly path.
    path = monthly_run_rate_path(company)
    return pd.DataFrame({
        "company": company,
        "month": path.index.to_timestamp(how="end").normalize(),
        "run_rate": path.values,
        "trailing_6m_cmgr": (path / path.shift(TRAILING_MONTHS)) ** (1 / TRAILING_MONTHS) - 1,
        "yoy_growth": path / path.shift(12) - 1,
    }).dropna(subset=["trailing_6m_cmgr"]).reset_index(drop=True)


trailing = pd.concat([trailing_growth(c) for c in COMPANIES], ignore_index=True)

def plot_trailing_growth():
    # Trailing 6-month CMGR along the monthly path.
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 4.6))
    for company in COMPANIES:
        t = trailing[trailing["company"] == company]
        ax.plot(t["month"], t["trailing_6m_cmgr"] * 100, color=COMPANY_COLOURS[company], lw=2, label=company)
        last = t.iloc[-1]
        ax.annotate(f"{last['trailing_6m_cmgr'] * 100:.1f}%/month\n({last['month']:%b %Y})",
                    (last["month"], last["trailing_6m_cmgr"] * 100), textcoords="offset points", xytext=(6, 0),
                    fontsize=8.5, color=COMPANY_COLOURS[company], va="center")
    ax.set_ylabel("Trailing 6-month CMGR (% per month)")
    ax.set_xlabel("Month (end of the 6-month window)")
    ax.set_title("Is growth slowing? Trailing 6-month growth of the reported run-rate", loc="left", fontsize=12)
    ax.grid(True, color="#dddddd", lw=0.7)
    ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
    ax.legend(loc="upper left", fontsize=9, frameon=False)
    ax.set_xlim(right=trailing["month"].max() + pd.Timedelta(days=75))
    fig.text(0.01, -0.02,
             "Built from log-linear interpolation between reported run-rates (2.2), so it smooths the interval CMGRs in 2.1 "
             "rather than adding data.",
             fontsize=8.5, color="#444444", va="top")
    plt.tight_layout()
    return fig


def decay_summary(company):
    t = trailing[trailing["company"] == company].set_index("month")
    last = t.index[-1]
    at = lambda k: t["trailing_6m_cmgr"].get(last - pd.offsets.MonthEnd(k), np.nan)
    return {"company": company, "latest month": f"{last:%b %Y}",
            "trailing 6m CMGR now": pct(at(0)), "6 months earlier": pct(at(6)), "12 months earlier": pct(at(12)),
            "peak (month)": f"{pct(t['trailing_6m_cmgr'].max())} ({t['trailing_6m_cmgr'].idxmax():%b %Y})",
            "year-on-year growth now": pct(t["yoy_growth"].iloc[-1], 0)}

           note="run_rate is interpolated (an estimate) except in months with a reported figure.")


S2_METRICS = [  # (metric, unit, how derived): the same definitions for both companies
    ("latest_run_rate", "USD_bn", "reported; month and source differ by company (see s1_key_figures)"),
    ("latest_run_rate_basis", "text", "revenue_basis of the latest run-rate (gross or net)"),
    ("latest_interval_cmgr", "fraction/month", "CMGR between the last two reported run-rates (2.1)"),
    ("latest_interval_annualised", "fraction/year", "(1 + latest interval CMGR)^12 - 1"),
    ("trailing_6m_cmgr", "fraction/month", "log-linear path, 6 months to the latest run-rate month (2.5)"),
    ("trailing_6m_annualised", "fraction/year", "(1 + trailing 6m CMGR)^12 - 1"),
    ("doubling_time_months", "months", "ln 2 / ln(1 + trailing 6m CMGR)"),
    ("fy2025_booked_reported", "USD_bn", "reported (Section 1)"),
    ("fy2025_booked_bridge_estimate", "USD_bn", "estimate (log-linear bridge), not reported"),
    ("fy2025_bridge_error", "fraction", "bridge estimate / reported - 1"),
    ("bridge_mean_abs_error_all_tests", "fraction", "log method, all bridge tests, both companies (2.2)"),
    ("ytd_2026_booked_estimate", "USD_bn", "estimate (log-linear bridge), not reported; Jan to latest run-rate month"),
] + [
    (f"run_rate_net_equiv_{round(h * 100)}pct", "USD_bn", f"latest run-rate less {pct(h, 0)} if reported gross ({label}; grade {grade})")
    for h, label, grade in HAIRCUTS[1:]
]


def s2_values(company):
    # Section 2's headline outputs for one company, in S2_METRICS order.
    g = growth[growth["company"] == company].iloc[-1]
    t = trailing[trailing["company"] == company].iloc[-1]
    rr = latest_rr[company]
    fy25 = tests[(tests["company"] == company) & (tests["period"] == "full year to 2025-12")]
    fy25_value = lambda col: fy25[col].iloc[0] if len(fy25) else np.nan
    ytd = bridge_estimates[(bridge_estimates["company"] == company)
                           & bridge_estimates["period"].str.startswith("2026 YTD")].iloc[0]
    basis = revenue_model.query("company == @company and type == 'run_rate'").sort_values("period_end")["revenue_basis"].iloc[-1]
    values = [
        rr["value"], basis, g["cmgr"], g["annualised"], t["trailing_6m_cmgr"], (1 + t["trailing_6m_cmgr"]) ** 12 - 1,
        np.log(2) / np.log(1 + t["trailing_6m_cmgr"]),
        fy25_value("reported_usd_bn"), fy25_value("est_log"), fy25_value("err_log"),
        bridge_error.loc["log", "mean absolute error"], ytd["estimate_usd_bn"],
    ] + [rr["value"] * (1 - h) if basis == "gross" else rr["value"] for h, _, _ in HAIRCUTS[1:]]
    return values


s2_growth = pd.DataFrame(S2_METRICS, columns=["metric", "unit", "how_derived"]).set_index("metric")
for c in COMPANIES:
    s2_growth[c] = s2_values(c)
s2_growth = s2_growth[COMPANIES + ["unit", "how_derived"]]


def fmt_s2(value, unit):
    if unit == "text":
        return value
    if pd.isna(value):
        return "n/a"
    if unit.startswith("fraction"):
        return pct(value)
    if unit == "USD_bn":
        return f"${value:,.1f}B"
    return f"{value:.1f}"


s2_display = s2_growth.copy()
for c in COMPANIES:

s1_fy24 = s1_derived.set_index("company").loc["Anthropic"]

show_table(leak_vs_runrate, "Leaked S-1 vs our run-rate picture (Anthropic)", collapsed=False,
           note="Draft S-1 figures are grade B (leaked draft via Reuters/FT), not audited. Bridge = log-linear run-rate bridge from 2.2.")


def growth_now_lines():
    # One line per company: monthly growth between its latest two reported run-rates, and the doubling time at that pace.
    out = []
    for c in COMPANIES:
        g = growth[growth["company"] == c].iloc[-1]
        out.append(f"- **{c}:** about {pct(g['cmgr'])} a month ({g['start']:%b} to {g['end']:%b %Y}), "
                   f"so revenue doubles roughly every {g['doubling_months']:.0f} months at that pace.")
    return "\n".join(out)


def gross_net_table():
    # Anthropic's latest (gross) run-rate after 0%, 10% (Axios, B) and ~27% (OpenAI's claim, C) haircuts, vs OpenAI's (net).
    an, oa = latest_rr["Anthropic"], latest_rr["OpenAI"]
    cases = [("As reported (gross)", 0.0, "-"),
             ("After a 10% haircut (Axios, high end)", ev.loc["net_switch_haircut_high", "value"] / 100, ev.loc["net_switch_haircut_high", "grade"]),
             (f"After a {claim_haircut:.0%} haircut (OpenAI's own claim)", claim_haircut, f"{claim['grade']}: sensitivity only")]
    return pd.DataFrame([{"case": label, "grade": g, f"Anthropic ({an['period_end']:%b %Y})": f"${an['value'] * (1 - h):.1f}B",
                          f"OpenAI ({oa['period_end']:%b %Y})": f"${oa['value']:g}B",
                          "Anthropic still ahead?": "yes" if an["value"] * (1 - h) > oa["value"] else "no"} for label, h, g in cases])


capture_to(None)

2.1 How fast?¶

Run-rates are reported at uneven intervals, so I use the compounded monthly growth rate (CMGR): the steady monthly growth rate that gets you from A to B.

CMGR = /(end ÷ start)^(1 ÷ months) − 1/

The chart shows the average monthly growth over the previous six months. Below it is each company's pace between its two latest reported run-rates.

▶ Show code
show_figure(plot_trailing_growth(), "Trailing 6-month growth")
display(Markdown(growth_now_lines()))
  • OpenAI: about 9.1% a month (Dec to Aug 2026), so revenue doubles roughly every 8 months at that pace.
  • Anthropic: about 17.6% a month (May to Jul 2026), so revenue doubles roughly every 4 months at that pace.

2.2 Can I trust the numbers?¶

Two checks:

  • The run-rate test. I rebuilt each company's FY2025 revenue from its run-rates and compared it with the real figure. It came in about 11% low for both, so run-rates are, if anything, conservative.
  • Gross vs net. Anthropic's figures include its cloud partners' cut. The table shrinks Anthropic's latest run-rate by 10% (a major outlet's estimate) and by 27% (OpenAI's own claim: a rival's view, so grade C).
▶ Show code
show_table(gross_net_table(), "Gross vs net: does Anthropic's lead survive?", collapsed=False)
▶ Show table: Gross vs net: does Anthropic's lead survive? (3 rows)
case grade Anthropic (Jul 2026) OpenAI (Aug 2026) Anthropic still ahead?
As reported (gross) - $65.0B $40B yes
After a 10% haircut (Axios, high end) B $58.5B $40B yes
After a 27% haircut (OpenAI's own claim) C: sensitivity only $47.7B $40B yes

2.3 Are they slowing down?¶

OpenAI has slowed a little, from about 11% a month to about 9%. Anthropic's six-month average still looks fast because it includes a spring surge, but its latest two-month pace dropped to about 18% a month. One data point isn't a trend yet.

Company forecasts: Anthropic's are already out of date: its estimated revenue for the first seven months of 2026 already beats its $18B forecast for the whole year. OpenAI's $350B target for 2030 needs about 65–76% growth a year from today's $40B run-rate.

▶ Show code
show_table(decay[["company", "trailing 6m CMGR now", "6 months earlier", "12 months earlier"]],
           "Is growth slowing? (average monthly growth over the previous 6 months)", collapsed=False)
▶ Show table: Is growth slowing? (average monthly growth over the previous 6 months) (2 rows)
company trailing 6m CMGR now 6 months earlier 12 months earlier
OpenAI 9.1% 11.2% 11.1%
Anthropic 34.0% 19.4% 23.0%

Key Takeaways¶

  • Compounded Monthly Growth Rates can be used to manage uneven run-rate reporting.
  • It is crucial to compare reported and reconstructed figures.
  • Anthropic's revenue figures remains ahead of OpenAI's (even when changing for net profit using data from various grades of sources).
  • Additionally, Anthropic's CMGR has been rather erratic yet higher compared to OpenAI's CMGR which is lower yet far more stable.

3. Who's paying, what does it cost, and will the money last?¶

The question: What have investors paid, how much does each company lose to earn its revenue, and is there enough cash for what it has promised to spend?

▶ Show code

VAL_MARKERS = {"primary": "o", "strategic": "s", "tender": "D", "proposed round": "^", "IPO target": "*"}

def plot_funding_chart():
    # Valuation per transaction (log) and cumulative capital raised.
    fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(10, 7.6), sharex=True, gridspec_kw={"height_ratios": [3, 2]})

                        facecolor="white" if hollow else colour, edgecolor=colour, linewidth=1.5, zorder=3)

def run_rate_at(company, date):
    # Run-rate for the month of `date`: interpolated inside the reported path, latest reported after it.
    path = monthly_run_rate_path(company)
    m = pd.Period(date, freq="M")
    if m in path.index:
        return path.loc[m], "interpolated" if m not in run_rate_series(company)["period_end"].dt.to_period("M").values else "reported"
    if m > path.index[-1]:
        return path.iloc[-1], f"latest reported ({path.index[-1].strftime('%b %Y')})"
    return np.nan, "before first run-rate (GAP)"


def ttm_booked_at(company, date):
    # Estimated booked revenue for the 12 months before `date` (run-rate bridge, 2.2). NaN if outside the path.
    return estimate_booked_revenue(company, str(pd.Period(date, freq="M") - 1), 12)


def implied_multiples(f=funding):
    rows = []
    for r in f.dropna(subset=["headline_valuation_usd_bn"]).itertuples():
        rr, rr_basis = run_rate_at(r.company, r.date)
        ttm = ttm_booked_at(r.company, r.date)
        rows.append({"company": r.company, "date": r.date, "round": r.round, "type": r.type,
                     "valuation_usd_bn": r.headline_valuation_usd_bn, "valuation_basis": r.valuation_basis,
                     "run_rate_usd_bn": rr, "run_rate_basis": rr_basis, "x_run_rate": r.headline_valuation_usd_bn / rr,
                     "ttm_booked_est_usd_bn": ttm, "x_ttm_booked_est": r.headline_valuation_usd_bn / ttm, "grade": r.grade})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

def latest_booked(company, rev_type):
    d = revenue_model[(revenue_model["company"] == company) & (revenue_model["type"] == rev_type)].sort_values("period_end")
    return d.iloc[-1] if not d.empty else None


def price_multiples(company, label, valuation, grade):
    rr = latest_rr[company]
    q = latest_booked(company, "quarter_revenue")
    fy = latest_booked(company, "annual_revenue")
    return {"company": company, "price": label, "valuation_usd_bn": valuation, "price grade": grade,
            "x latest run-rate": f"{valuation / rr['value']:.1f}x (on ${rr['value']:g}B, {rr['period_end']:%b %Y})",
            "x latest booked quarter x4": "GAP" if q is None else
                f"{valuation / (4 * q['value']):.1f}x (on ${4 * q['value']:g}B, Q to {q['period']})",
            "x FY booked revenue": "GAP" if fy is None else f"{valuation / fy['value']:.0f}x (on ${fy['value']:g}B, FY{fy['period'][:4]})"}


def headline_prices(company):
    f = funding[(funding["company"] == company) & funding["headline_valuation_usd_bn"].notna()]
    paid = f[f["type"].isin(CLOSED_TYPES)].iloc[-1]
    out = [(f"Last price paid: {paid['round']} ({paid['date']:%b %Y})", paid["headline_valuation_usd_bn"], paid["grade"])]
    sought = f[f["type"].isin(["proposed round", "IPO target"])]
    for r in sought.itertuples():
        value = r.post_money_usd_bn if pd.notna(r.post_money_usd_bn) else r.headline_valuation_usd_bn
        basis = "post-money: pre-money + new money" if pd.notna(r.post_money_usd_bn) else r.valuation_basis
        out.append((f"Price sought: {r.round} ({r.date:%b %Y}; {basis})", value, r.grade))
    return out

def ev_bridge(company):
    paid = headline_prices(company)[0]
    cash = financials.query("company == @company and metric == 'cash_and_short_term_investments'").sort_values("period")
    c = cash.iloc[-1] if not cash.empty else None

            "less: cash (latest reported)": "GAP" if c is None else f"${c['value']:g}B at {c['period']} ({c['source_id']}, grade {c['grade']}); "
                                                                      "stale: before later raises",
            "plus: debt and debt-like claims": "GAP",
            "enterprise value": "GAP (needs cash and debt at the same date as the price)"}
