           note="EV = equity value - cash + debt. Needed later to compare a DCF (which values the operating business) with a round price.")


PERIODS = [  # (label, metric suffix in financials.csv, period, booked-revenue type)
    ("FY2024", "fy", "2024-12", "annual_revenue"), ("H1 2025", "h1", "2025-06", "half_year_revenue"),
    ("FY2025", "fy", "2025-12", "annual_revenue"), ("Q1 2026", "q", "2026-03", "quarter_revenue"),
    ("Q2 2026", "q", "2026-06", "quarter_revenue"),
]
UE_INPUTS = ["cost_of_revenue", "compute_infrastructure_spend", "operating_loss", "net_loss",
             "noncash_convertible_instrument_charge", "cash_burn", "gross_margin", "adjusted_gross_margin",
             "adjusted_operating_margin"]


def fin_value(company, metric, period, types=("reported", "adjusted")):
    d = financials[(financials["company"] == company) & (financials["metric"] == metric)
                   & (financials["period"] == period) & financials["figure_type"].isin(types)]
    return d.iloc[0] if not d.empty else None


def booked_revenue(company, rev_type, period):
    d = revenue_model[(revenue_model["company"] == company) & (revenue_model["type"] == rev_type) & (revenue_model["period"] == period)]
    if not d.empty:
        return d.iloc[0]["value"], f"reported ({d.iloc[0]['source_id']}, grade {d.iloc[0]['grade']})"
    derived = derived_prior_year_revenue(company, int(period[:4])) if rev_type == "annual_revenue" else None
    if derived:
        return derived["derived_usd_bn"], "derived (next FY / growth multiple)"
    return np.nan, "GAP"


def unit_economics(company):
    rows = []
    for label, suffix, period, rev_type in PERIODS:
        rev, rev_source = booked_revenue(company, rev_type, period)
        row = {"company": company, "period": label, "revenue_usd_bn": rev, "revenue_source": rev_source}
        sources = []
        for m in UE_INPUTS:
            v = fin_value(company, f"{m}_{suffix}", period)
            row[m] = np.nan if v is None else (v["value"] / 100 if v["unit"] == "percent" else v["value"])
            if v is not None:
                sources.append(f"{v['source_id']}({v['grade']})")
        cash = fin_value(company, "cash_and_short_term_investments", period)
        row["cash_end_usd_bn"] = np.nan if cash is None else cash["value"]
        row["cost_of_revenue_pct_rev"] = row["cost_of_revenue"] / rev
        row["gaap_gross_margin"] = 1 - row["cost_of_revenue"] / rev
        row["compute_pct_rev"] = row["compute_infrastructure_spend"] / rev
        row["operating_margin"] = -row["operating_loss"] / rev
        row["net_margin"] = -row["net_loss"] / rev
        row["cash_burn_pct_rev"] = row["cash_burn"] / rev
        row["sources"] = ", ".join(sorted(set(sources))) or "none"
        rows.append(row)
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


s3_unit_economics = pd.concat([unit_economics(c) for c in COMPANIES], ignore_index=True)
RATIO_COLS = ["gross_margin", "adjusted_gross_margin", "adjusted_operating_margin", "cost_of_revenue_pct_rev", "gaap_gross_margin",
              "compute_pct_rev", "operating_margin", "net_margin", "cash_burn_pct_rev"]
ue_display = s3_unit_economics.copy()
for col in RATIO_COLS:
    ue_display[col] = ue_display[col].map(lambda x: "GAP" if pd.isna(x) else pct(x, 0))
show_table(ue_display.fillna("GAP"), "Unit economics by period, both companies (s3_unit_economics)",
           note="Money in USD bn, ratios as % of booked revenue for the same period. GAP = not reported. "
                "gross_margin = margin the company reported to investors; adjusted_* = company's own definition.")

KEY_UE = [("revenue_usd_bn", "Booked revenue (USD bn)"), ("compute_infrastructure_spend", "Compute & infrastructure spend (USD bn)"),
          ("compute_pct_rev", "Compute / revenue"), ("cost_of_revenue_pct_rev", "Cost of revenue / revenue"),
          ("gaap_gross_margin", "Gross margin from statements"), ("adjusted_gross_margin", "Adjusted gross margin (company definition)"),
          ("operating_margin", "Operating margin"), ("net_margin", "Net margin (incl. non-cash charges)"),
          ("cash_burn_pct_rev", "Cash burn / revenue"), ("cash_end_usd_bn", "Cash at year end (USD bn)")]


def key_ue_table(period="FY2025"):
    ue = s3_unit_economics[s3_unit_economics["period"] == period].set_index("company")
    out = []
    for col, label in KEY_UE:
        row = {"metric": label}
        for c in COMPANIES:
            v = ue.loc[c, col]
            row[c] = "GAP" if pd.isna(v) else (pct(v, 0) if col in RATIO_COLS else f"{v:,.2f}")
        out.append(row)
    return pd.DataFrame(out)


show_table(key_ue_table("FY2025"), "FY2025 side by side", collapsed=False,
           note="Compute/revenue (Anthropic) and cost of revenue/revenue (OpenAI) measure different cost pools: not comparable.")


def exit_run_rate(company, year):
    path = monthly_run_rate_path(company)
    m = pd.Period(f"{year}-12", freq="M")
    return path.loc[m] if m in path.index else np.nan


def burn_multiples(company, year=2025):
    ue = s3_unit_economics.set_index(["company", "period"])
    fy, prev = ue.loc[(company, f"FY{year}")], ue.loc[(company, f"FY{year - 1}")]
    new_arr = exit_run_rate(company, year) - exit_run_rate(company, year - 1)
    new_booked = fy["revenue_usd_bn"] - prev["revenue_usd_bn"]
    return {"company": company, "year": year,
            "cash burn (USD bn)": fy["cash_burn"], "operating loss (USD bn)": fy["operating_loss"],
            "net new ARR, Dec-Dec (USD bn)": new_arr, "net new booked revenue (USD bn)": new_booked,
            "burn multiple (cash / new ARR)": fy["cash_burn"] / new_arr,
            "burn multiple (cash / new booked)": fy["cash_burn"] / new_booked,
            "proxy: op. loss / new ARR": fy["operating_loss"] / new_arr,
            "proxy: op. loss / new booked": fy["operating_loss"] / new_booked,
            "prior-year revenue basis": prev["revenue_source"]}


burn = pd.DataFrame([burn_multiples(c) for c in COMPANIES])
show_table(burn.round(2).fillna("GAP"), "Burn multiple, FY2025", collapsed=False,
           note="Proxy rows use operating loss, not cash: labelled, for symmetry only. Anthropic's FY2024 revenue is derived (Section 1.6).")


def capital_efficiency(company):
    f = funding[funding["company"] == company]
    cap_2025 = f.loc[f["date"] <= "2025-12-31", "amount_counted_usd_bn"].sum()
    cap_now = f["amount_counted_usd_bn"].sum()
    fy25 = s3_unit_economics.query("company == @company and period == 'FY2025'")["revenue_usd_bn"].iloc[0]
    rr = latest_rr[company]["value"]
    return {"company": company, "capital counted to end-2025 (USD bn)": cap_2025, "FY2025 revenue (USD bn)": fy25,
            "FY2025 revenue per $ of capital": fy25 / cap_2025,
            "capital counted to date (USD bn)": cap_now, "latest run-rate (USD bn)": rr,
            "run-rate per $ of capital": rr / cap_now}


show_table(pd.DataFrame([capital_efficiency(c) for c in COMPANIES]).round(2), "Revenue per $ of capital raised (since 2023)",
           collapsed=False, note="Capital counted as in 3.1: no tenders, no double counting, no contingent tranches; pre-2023 money excluded.")


def loss_reconciliation(company, year=2025):
    ue = s3_unit_economics.set_index(["company", "period"]).loc[(company, f"FY{year}")]
    net, charge, op = -ue["net_loss"], ue["noncash_convertible_instrument_charge"], -ue["operating_loss"]
    ex_charge = net + charge
    adj = financials.query("company == @company and metric == 'adjusted_operating_profit_q'").sort_values("period")
    adj_txt = "GAP" if adj.empty else (f"{adj.iloc[-1]['value']:+.2f} ({adj.iloc[-1]['figure_type']}, quarter to {adj.iloc[-1]['period']}, "
                                       f"{adj.iloc[-1]['source_id']}; excludes stock-based pay)")
    fmt = lambda v: "GAP" if pd.isna(v) else f"{v:+,.2f}"
    return pd.DataFrame({
        "step": ["1. Net profit / (loss), GAAP", "2. Add back: non-cash convertible / fair-value charge",
                 "   = Profit / (loss) excluding that charge", "3. Operating profit / (loss)",
                 "   Residual: other non-operating items (interest, investment gains, tax)",
                 "4. Latest adjusted operating profit (different period)"],
        company: [fmt(net), fmt(charge), fmt(ex_charge), fmt(op), fmt(ex_charge - op), adj_txt]}).set_index("step")


recon = pd.concat([loss_reconciliation(c) for c in COMPANIES], axis=1).reset_index()
show_table(recon, "FY2025: from net loss to operating loss (USD bn, + = profit)", collapsed=False,
           note="Inputs approximate where sources say 'roughly'/'nearly' (Anthropic). The residual is unexplained by our sources: a GAP.")


concentration = pd.read_csv(DATA_DIR / "concentration.csv").merge(
    source_log[["source_id", "company", "grade"]].rename(columns={"company": "source_company"}),
    on="source_id", how="left", validate="many_to_one", indicator=True)
assert (concentration["_merge"] == "both").all(), "concentration.csv row with no matching source in source_log"
concentration = concentration.drop(columns="_merge")
assert (concentration["source_company"].isin(["Both"]) | (concentration["source_company"] == concentration["company"])).all()
assert concentration["unit"].isin(["USD_billions", "percent", "text"]).all()

BURN_MONTHS = {"cash_burn_q": 3, "cash_burn_h1": 6, "cash_burn_fy": 12}


def latest_cash(company):
    d = financials.query("company == @company and metric == 'cash_and_short_term_investments' and figure_type == 'reported'").sort_values("period")
    return d.iloc[-1] if not d.empty else None


def latest_monthly_burn(company):
    d = financials[(financials["company"] == company) & financials["metric"].isin(BURN_MONTHS)].sort_values("period")
    if not d.empty:
        r = d.iloc[-1]
        return r["value"] / BURN_MONTHS[r["metric"]], f"cash burn, {r['metric'][10:].upper()} to {r['period']} ({r['source_id']}, {r['grade']})"
    d = financials.query("company == @company and metric == 'operating_loss_fy' and figure_type == 'reported'").sort_values("period")
    r = d.iloc[-1]
    return r["value"] / 12, f"PROXY: FY operating loss to {r['period']} / 12 (cash burn is a GAP)"


def capital_needs(company):
    commit = financials.query("company == @company and metric == 'future_compute_commitments'").sort_values("period").iloc[-1]
    cash = latest_cash(company)
    since = pd.Timestamp(cash["period"]) + pd.offsets.MonthEnd(0) if cash is not None else pd.Timestamp("2025-12-31")
    raised = funding.loc[(funding["company"] == company) & (funding["date"] > since), "amount_counted_usd_bn"].sum()
    available = (cash["value"] if cash is not None else 0) + raised
    burn_m, burn_basis = latest_monthly_burn(company)
    rr = latest_rr[company]["value"]
    return {"company": company,
            "compute commitments (USD bn)": commit["value"], "commitments as stated": f"{commit['notes']} ({commit['source_id']}, {commit['grade']})",
            "last reported cash (USD bn)": "GAP" if cash is None else f"{cash['value']:g} at {cash['period']}",
            f"capital counted since {since:%b %Y} (USD bn)": raised,
            "cash available (USD bn)": available if cash is not None else f">= {available:g} (lower bound: cash GAP)",
            "monthly burn (USD bn)": round(burn_m, 2), "burn basis": burn_basis,
            "runway (months, snapshot)": f"{available / burn_m:.0f}" + ("" if cash is not None else "+ (lower bound)"),
            "commitments / cash available": f"{commit['value'] / available:.1f}x" + ("" if cash is not None else " (upper bound)"),
            "commitments / latest run-rate (years of revenue)": round(commit["value"] / rr, 1)}


cap_needs = pd.DataFrame([capital_needs(c) for c in COMPANIES]).set_index("company").T
cap_needs.columns.name = None
cap_needs = cap_needs.reset_index().rename(columns={"index": "item"})
show_table(cap_needs, "Commitments vs cash, burn and revenue (snapshot, not a forecast)", collapsed=False,
           note="Commitment horizons differ: OpenAI's ~$1.4T is over 8 years; Anthropic's $518B horizon is not stated in reports. "
                "Anthropic's burn is a labelled proxy; its 2026 quarters are reported as profitable on an adjusted basis.")

plans = financials[financials["metric"].isin(["future_compute_commitments", "compute_and_infrastructure_spend_through_2030",
                                               "cumulative_free_cash_flow_2026_2030"])]
plans = pd.concat([plans, concentration.query("item == 'cloud_partner_commitment' and unit == 'USD_billions'").rename(columns={"item": "metric"})
                   .assign(figure_type="commitment (subset)")], ignore_index=True)
show_table(plans[["company", "metric", "figure_type", "period", "value", "source_id", "notes"]].sort_values(["company", "period"]),
           "All reported spending plans and commitments",
           note="Different scopes and horizons: they are listed, not added up. Partner-specific commitments are subsets of the totals.")


def own_projection_burn(company):
    # Cumulative cash the company itself projects to burn before break-even (same function, whichever data exists).
    fcf = financials.query("company == @company and metric == 'cumulative_free_cash_flow_2026_2030' and figure_type == 'projection'")
    if not fcf.empty:
        r = fcf.iloc[-1]
        return -r["value"], f"own cumulative FCF 2026-2030 = {r['value']:g} ({r['source_id']}, {r['grade']})"
    pcts = financials.query("company == @company and metric == 'cash_burn_pct_revenue_fy' and figure_type == 'projection'")
    total, parts = 0.0, []
    for r in pcts.itertuples():
        proj = revenue_model.query("company == @company and type == 'projection' and period == @r.period")
        if proj.empty:
            return np.nan, f"GAP: no revenue projection for {r.period}"
        p = proj.sort_values("date_published").iloc[-1]
        total += r.value / 100 * p["value"]
        parts.append(f"{r.value:g}% x ${p['value']:g}B ({r.period[:4]})")
    return (total, "own burn % x own revenue forecasts: " + " + ".join(parts)) if parts else (np.nan, "GAP")


def funding_gap(company):
    needs = capital_needs(company)
    available = needs["cash available (USD bn)"]
    lower_bound = isinstance(available, str)
    avail_num = float(available.split()[1]) if lower_bound else available
    burn_total, basis = own_projection_burn(company)
    commit = needs["compute commitments (USD bn)"]
    return {"company": company, "projected burn to break-even (USD bn)": burn_total, "basis": basis,
            "cash available (USD bn)": avail_num, "cash available is a lower bound": lower_bound,
            "gap on own projections (USD bn)": max(0.0, burn_total - avail_num),
            "stress: commitments - cash available (USD bn)": max(0.0, commit - avail_num)}


gaps3 = pd.DataFrame([funding_gap(c) for c in COMPANIES])
show_table(gaps3.round(1), "Funding gap if each company's OWN projections come true", collapsed=False,
           note="Illustrative arithmetic, not a forecast. 'Stress' pretends the commitments were paid entirely from new capital "
                "with zero revenue: an upper bound, not a scenario. Where cash is a lower bound, the gap is an upper bound.")


def dilution_table(company):
    g = gaps3.set_index("company").loc[company]
    f = funding[(funding["company"] == company) & funding["headline_valuation_usd_bn"].notna()]
    paid = f[f["type"].isin(CLOSED_TYPES)].iloc[-1]["headline_valuation_usd_bn"]
    sought = f[f["type"].isin(["proposed round", "IPO target"])].iloc[-1]["headline_valuation_usd_bn"]
    rows = []
    for case, gap in [("Gap on own projections", g["gap on own projections (USD bn)"]),
                      ("Stress: commitments - cash", g["stress: commitments - cash available (USD bn)"])]:
        row = {"company": company, "case": case, "capital to raise (USD bn)": round(gap, 1)}
        for label, pre in [("last price paid", paid), ("price sought", sought), ("half the price sought", sought / 2)]:
            row[f"at {label}"] = (pct(gap / (pre + gap)) if gap > 0 else "0% (no gap)") + f" (pre-money ${pre:,.0f}B)"
        rows.append(row)
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


show_table(pd.concat([dilution_table(c) for c in COMPANIES], ignore_index=True),
           "ILLUSTRATIVE dilution: share of the company new money would buy", collapsed=False,
           note="Share new investors would own = capital / (pre-money + capital). Illustrative arithmetic only, not a forecast of any raise. "
                "Anthropic's price sought is an IPO target, used here as if it were a pre-money price.")


CONCENTRATION_ITEMS = [  # (question, table, metric/item): same five questions for both companies
    ("1. Top-customer share of revenue", "financials", "top2_customer_revenue_share"),
    ("2. Long-term contract coverage", "concentration", "long_term_contract_coverage"),
    ("3. Business vs consumer mix", "concentration", "business_share_of_revenue"),
    ("4. Compute / cloud partner dependence", "concentration", "cloud_partner_commitment"),
    ("5. Distribution-partner economics", "concentration", "distribution_partner_economics"),
]


def concentration_cell(company, table, key):
    if table == "financials":
        d = financials.query("company == @company and metric == @key")
    else:
        d = concentration.query("company == @company and item == @key")
    if d.empty:
        return "GAP"
    parts = []
    for r in d.itertuples():
        value = "" if pd.isna(r.value) else (f"{r.value:g}% " if r.unit == "percent" else f"${r.value:g}B " if r.unit == "USD_billions" else "")
        parts.append(f"{value}{r.notes} [{r.source_id}, grade {r.grade}]".strip())
    return " | ".join(parts)


concentration_table = pd.DataFrame([{"question": q, **{c: concentration_cell(c, t, k) for c in COMPANIES}}
                                    for q, t, k in CONCENTRATION_ITEMS])
show_table(concentration_table, "Concentration and contract risk: same five questions", collapsed=False,
           note="GAP = not disclosed in any A/B source we found. Anthropic has more answers mainly because its draft S-1 leaked.")


GRADE_ORDER = {"A": 0, "B": 1, "C": 2}


def weakest(*grades):
    gs = [g for g in grades if isinstance(g, str) and g in GRADE_ORDER]
    return max(gs, key=GRADE_ORDER.get) if gs else "-"


def fin_grade(company, metric, period=None):
    d = financials.query("company == @company and metric == @metric")
    if period:
        d = d[d["period"] == period]
    return d.iloc[-1]["grade"] if not d.empty else None


def scorecard_values(company):
    f = funding[(funding["company"] == company) & funding["headline_valuation_usd_bn"].notna()]
    paid = f[f["type"].isin(CLOSED_TYPES)].iloc[-1]
    sought = f[f["type"].isin(["proposed round", "IPO target"])].iloc[-1]
    paid_mult = multiples[(multiples["company"] == company) & (multiples["date"] == paid["date"]) & (multiples["round"] == paid["round"])].iloc[0]
    rr = latest_rr[company]
    fy25 = s3_unit_economics.set_index(["company", "period"]).loc[(company, "FY2025")]
    fy25_grade = revenue_model.query("company == @company and type == 'annual_revenue' and period == '2025-12'")["grade"].iloc[0]
    b = burn.set_index("company").loc[company]
    cash = latest_cash(company)
    needs = capital_needs(company)
    commit = needs["compute commitments (USD bn)"]
    avail = needs["cash available (USD bn)"]
    top = financials.query("company == @company and metric == 'top2_customer_revenue_share'")
    basis = revenue_model.query("company == @company and type == 'run_rate'").sort_values("period_end").iloc[-1]
    return [  # (metric, value, unit, grade)
        ("Latest price paid (post-money)", paid["headline_valuation_usd_bn"], "USD_bn", paid["grade"]),
        ("Price sought (IPO target / round in talks)", sought["headline_valuation_usd_bn"], "USD_bn", sought["grade"]),
        ("Price paid / run-rate at that date", paid_mult["x_run_rate"], "x", weakest(paid["grade"], rr["grade"])),
        ("Price sought / latest run-rate", sought["headline_valuation_usd_bn"] / rr["value"], "x", weakest(sought["grade"], rr["grade"])),
        ("Price paid / FY2025 booked revenue", paid["headline_valuation_usd_bn"] / fy25["revenue_usd_bn"], "x", weakest(paid["grade"], fy25_grade)),
        ("Compute spend / revenue (FY2025)", fy25["compute_pct_rev"], "fraction", fin_grade(company, "compute_infrastructure_spend_fy", "2025-12")),
        ("Cost of revenue / revenue (FY2025)", fy25["cost_of_revenue_pct_rev"], "fraction", fin_grade(company, "cost_of_revenue_fy", "2025-12")),
        ("Operating margin (FY2025)", fy25["operating_margin"], "fraction", weakest(fin_grade(company, "operating_loss_fy", "2025-12"), fy25_grade)),
        ("Burn multiple (FY2025 cash burn / new ARR)", b["burn multiple (cash / new ARR)"], "x", fin_grade(company, "cash_burn_fy", "2025-12")),
        ("Cash (latest reported)", np.nan if cash is None else cash["value"], "USD_bn", None if cash is None else cash["grade"]),
        ("Compute commitments", commit, "USD_bn", fin_grade(company, "future_compute_commitments")),
        ("Commitments / cash available", np.nan if isinstance(avail, str) else commit / avail, "x",
         None if isinstance(avail, str) else weakest(fin_grade(company, "future_compute_commitments"), cash["grade"])),
        ("Top-customer concentration", np.nan if top.empty else top.iloc[0]["value"] / 100, "fraction", None if top.empty else top.iloc[0]["grade"]),
        ("Revenue basis (gross / net)", basis["revenue_basis"], "text", "B"),
    ]


def fmt_score(value, unit, grade):
    if unit != "text" and pd.isna(value):
        return "GAP"
    text = value if unit == "text" else (f"${value:,.0f}B" if unit == "USD_bn" and value >= 100 else f"${value:,.2f}B" if unit == "USD_bn"
                                         else f"{value:,.1f}x" if unit == "x" else pct(value, 0))
    return f"{text} ({grade})" if grade else text


score_rows = {c: scorecard_values(c) for c in COMPANIES}
s3_scorecard = pd.DataFrame({"metric": [m for m, *_ in score_rows[COMPANIES[0]]], "unit": [u for _, _, u, _ in score_rows[COMPANIES[0]]]})
for c in COMPANIES:
    s3_scorecard[c] = [v for _, v, _, _ in score_rows[c]]
    s3_scorecard[f"{c}_grade"] = [g if not (u != "text" and pd.isna(v)) else "GAP" for _, v, u, g in score_rows[c]]
s3_scorecard = s3_scorecard.set_index("metric")

show_table(pd.DataFrame({"metric": s3_scorecard.index,
                         **{c: [fmt_score(v, u, g) for _, v, u, g in score_rows[c]] for c in COMPANIES}}),
           "Scorecard: OpenAI vs Anthropic (s3_scorecard)", collapsed=False,
           note="Grade in brackets; computed cells take the weakest input grade. 'Cash available' = last reported cash + capital counted since. "
                "Anthropic's revenue is gross and OpenAI's net, which flatters Anthropic's revenue multiples relative to OpenAI's (2.4).")


def fin_points(company, metric, types):
    d = financials.query("company == @company and metric == @metric and figure_type in @types").sort_values("period")
    return [(r.value, f"{r.value:g}{'%' if r.unit == 'percent' else ''} ({r.period[:4]}{'' if r.figure_type == 'reported' else ', ' + r.figure_type}; {r.source_id})")
            for r in d.itertuples()]


def ue_points(company, col):
    d = s3_unit_economics[(s3_unit_economics["company"] == company) & s3_unit_economics[col].notna()]
    return [(v * 100, f"{v * 100:.0f}% ({p})") for v, p in zip(d[col], d["period"])]


def mult_points(company, col):
    d = multiples[(multiples["company"] == company) & multiples["type"].isin(CLOSED_TYPES) & multiples[col].notna()]
    return [(v, f"{v:.0f}x ({r} {dt:%b %Y})") for v, r, dt in zip(d[col], d["round"], d["date"])]


def projected_operating_result(company):
    # Projected operating profit (+) or loss (-), in USD bn, from loss and adjusted-profit projections.
    d = financials.query("company == @company and figure_type == 'projection' and metric in ['operating_loss_fy', 'adjusted_operating_profit_q']")
    return [((-r.value if r.metric == "operating_loss_fy" else r.value),
             f"{(-r.value if r.metric == 'operating_loss_fy' else r.value):+g}B ({'FY' if r.metric.endswith('_fy') else 'quarter to '}{r.period[:4] if r.metric.endswith('_fy') else r.period}; {r.source_id})")
            for r in d.itertuples()]


RANGE_SPECS = [  # (range, how to collect points for one company)
    ("Gross margin: actual / adjusted (%)", lambda c: fin_points(c, "gross_margin_fy", ["reported"]) + fin_points(c, "adjusted_gross_margin_fy", ["adjusted"])
                                                      + ue_points(c, "gaap_gross_margin")),
    ("Gross margin: projected (%)", lambda c: fin_points(c, "gross_margin_fy", ["projection"]) + fin_points(c, "adjusted_gross_margin_fy", ["projection"])),
    ("Compute spend / revenue (%)", lambda c: ue_points(c, "compute_pct_rev")),
    ("Cost of revenue / revenue (%)", lambda c: ue_points(c, "cost_of_revenue_pct_rev")),
    ("Operating margin: actual (%)", lambda c: ue_points(c, "operating_margin") + fin_points(c, "adjusted_operating_margin_q", ["adjusted"])),
    ("Operating result: projected (USD bn)", lambda c: projected_operating_result(c)),
    ("Cash burn / revenue: actual (%)", lambda c: ue_points(c, "cash_burn_pct_rev")),
    ("Cash burn / revenue: projected (%)", lambda c: fin_points(c, "cash_burn_pct_revenue_fy", ["projection"])),
    ("Break-even year: projected", lambda c: fin_points(c, "breakeven_year", ["projection"])),
    ("Price paid / run-rate at the time (x)", lambda c: mult_points(c, "x_run_rate")),
    ("Price paid / trailing-12m booked estimate (x)", lambda c: mult_points(c, "x_ttm_booked_est")),
    ("Long-range revenue projections (USD bn)", lambda c: [(r.value, f"${r.value:g}B FY{r.period[:4]} ({r.source_id})") for r in
                                                           revenue_model.query("company == @c and type == 'projection' and period >= '2028-01'").itertuples()]),
]


def range_row(name, collect):
    row = {"range": name}
    for c in COMPANIES:
        pts = collect(c)
        if not pts:
            row[f"{c} low-high"], row[f"{c} observations"] = "GAP", "GAP"
            continue
        vals = [v for v, _ in pts]
        num = lambda v: f"{round(v):d}" if abs(v) >= 10 else f"{v:.2f}"
        row[f"{c} low-high"] = num(min(vals)) if min(vals) == max(vals) else f"{num(min(vals))} to {num(max(vals))}"
        row[f"{c} observations"] = "; ".join(lbl for _, lbl in pts)
    return row


s3_ranges = pd.DataFrame([range_row(n, f) for n, f in RANGE_SPECS])
show_table(s3_ranges, "Observed and projected ranges for Section 5 (no choices made)",
           note="Actual, adjusted and projected values are kept in separate rows. Multiples use prices actually paid only; "
                "the trailing-12m booked estimate is ~11% low (2.2), so those multiples are somewhat high.")


def price_table():
    # Last price paid, price being sought, and both as a multiple of the latest run-rate.
    rows = []
    for c in COMPANIES:
        f = funding[(funding["company"] == c) & funding["headline_valuation_usd_bn"].notna()]
        paid = f[f["type"].isin(CLOSED_TYPES)].iloc[-1]
        sought = f[f["type"].isin(["proposed round", "IPO target"])].iloc[-1]
        rr = latest_rr[c]["value"]
        rows.append({"company": c,
                     "last price paid": f"${paid['headline_valuation_usd_bn']:,.0f}B ({paid['date']:%b %Y}, grade {paid['grade']})",
                     "price sought": f"${sought['headline_valuation_usd_bn']:,.0f}B ({sought['date']:%b %Y}, grade {sought['grade']})",
                     "last price / latest run-rate": f"{paid['headline_valuation_usd_bn'] / rr:.0f}x",
                     "price sought / latest run-rate": f"{sought['headline_valuation_usd_bn'] / rr:.0f}x"})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def fy2025_table():
    # FY2025: revenue, operating loss, operating loss as % of revenue, cash burn (GAP if not reported).
    ue = s3_unit_economics[s3_unit_economics["period"] == "FY2025"].set_index("company")
    usd = lambda v: "GAP" if pd.isna(v) else f"${v:,.1f}B"
    return pd.DataFrame([{"company": c, "revenue": usd(ue.loc[c, "revenue_usd_bn"]), "operating loss": usd(ue.loc[c, "operating_loss"]),
                          "operating loss as % of revenue": pct(ue.loc[c, "operating_loss"] / ue.loc[c, "revenue_usd_bn"], 0),
                          "cash burn": usd(ue.loc[c, "cash_burn"])} for c in COMPANIES])


def commitments_table():
    # Compute commitments vs cash available, in years of current revenue, and runway (snapshot).
    rows = []
    for c in COMPANIES:
        n = capital_needs(c)
        avail = n["cash available (USD bn)"]
        rows.append({"company": c, "compute commitments": f"${n['compute commitments (USD bn)']:,.0f}B",
                     "cash available": f"at least ${float(avail.split()[1]):,.0f}B (cash GAP)" if isinstance(avail, str) else f"${avail:,.0f}B",
                     "commitments in years of revenue": f"{n['commitments / latest run-rate (years of revenue)']:.0f}",
                     "runway (months, snapshot)": n["runway (months, snapshot)"]})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def customer_lines():
    # Two lines per company from the concentration data (GAP where unknown).
    q = concentration_table.set_index("question")
    out = []
    for c in COMPANIES:
        top, contracts, mix = (q.loc[k, c] for k in ["1. Top-customer share of revenue", "2. Long-term contract coverage", "3. Business vs consumer mix"])
        out.append(f"**{c}**\n\n- Biggest customers: {top}. Contracts: {contracts}.\n- Who pays: {mix}.\n")
    return "\n".join(out)


def scorecard_short():
    # Six headline rows from s3_scorecard (s3_scorecard itself is unchanged), plus commitments in years of revenue.
    keep = ["Latest price paid (post-money)", "Price sought (IPO target / round in talks)", "Price paid / run-rate at that date",
            "Operating margin (FY2025)", "Top-customer concentration"]
    rows = []
    for m in keep:
        grade = lambda c: None if s3_scorecard.loc[m, f"{c}_grade"] in ("GAP", "-") else s3_scorecard.loc[m, f"{c}_grade"]
        rows.append({"metric": m, **{c: fmt_score(s3_scorecard.loc[m, c], s3_scorecard.loc[m, "unit"], grade(c)) for c in COMPANIES}})
    years = {c: f"{capital_needs(c)['commitments / latest run-rate (years of revenue)']:.0f} years (B)" for c in COMPANIES}
    rows.insert(4, {"metric": "Compute commitments / latest run-rate", **years})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

3.1 What have investors paid?¶

The chart shows the price of each funding deal (top) and the total cash raised since 2023 (bottom). A round price is what someone paid for one kind of share on one day, not what the whole company is "worth". Some investors (Amazon, Nvidia, Microsoft, Google) also sell computing power to the company, so part of their money comes back to them.

▶ Show code
show_figure(plot_funding_chart(), "Valuations and capital raised")

company last price paid price sought last price / latest run-rate price sought / latest run-rate
OpenAI $852B (Mar 2026, grade A) $1,400B (Sep 2026, grade B) 21x 35x
Anthropic $965B (May 2026, grade A) $2,000B (Sep 2026, grade B) 15x 31x

3.2 Are they making money?¶

No: in 2025 both lost more than they earned in revenue. Most of the headline net losses ($42B for Anthropic, $38.5B for OpenAI) are non-cash accounting charges, so I focus on operating loss (revenue minus running costs) and cash burn (cash that actually left the company).

▶ Show code
show_table(fy2025_table(), "FY2025: are they making money?", collapsed=False)
▶ Show table: FY2025: are they making money? (2 rows)
company revenue operating loss operating loss as % of revenue cash burn
OpenAI $13.1B $20.9B 160% $8.0B
Anthropic $4.6B $8.1B 175% GAP

3.3 The big bet: compute commitments vs cash¶

Both companies have signed long contracts for computing power that dwarf the cash they hold. Runway = how many months the cash would last at the latest burn rate.

These contracts are fixed costs. If revenue keeps growing, profits will grow very fast; if it stalls, losses will deepen just as fast, because the bills don't shrink.

3.4 Who are the customers?¶

Revenue that depends on a few big customers, or on customers who can leave at short notice, can disappear quickly.

Key Takeaways¶

  • Round price = payment for one share on one particular day.
  • Most of the losses for these companies are non-cash accounting charges which are expenses which reduce reported net income without immediate cash outflows (such as depreciation and ammortization).
  • OpenAI has 35 years of commitments in terms of yearly revenue whereas Ahtnropic only has 8 years of commitment. Additionally, it is estimated that it would take only 71 months for OpenAI to burn through their commitments whereas it would take 172 months for Anthropic to burn through their commitments.

4. What people are saying¶

The question: What are executives, investors, analysts, critics and regulators saying about each company, and do their claims match my numbers?

def grade_mix(rows):
    counts = rows["grade"].value_counts().sort_index()
    return ", ".join(f"{g}x{n}" for g, n in counts.items())


def speaker_coverage(company):
    # Statements per speaker type for one company (GAP if none), plus shared statements about both companies.
    own, both = s4_statements[s4_statements["company"] == company], s4_statements[s4_statements["company"] == "Both"]
    out = {}
    for t in SPEAKER_TYPES:
        o, b = own[own["speaker_type"] == t], both[both["speaker_type"] == t]
        out[t] = ("GAP" if o.empty else f"{len(o)} ({grade_mix(o)})") + (f" + {len(b)} shared ({grade_mix(b)})" if len(b) else "")
    return out


coverage_table = pd.DataFrame({c: speaker_coverage(c) for c in COMPANIES}).rename_axis("speaker type").reset_index()
show_table(coverage_table, "Who is speaking: statements by speaker type and grade",
           note="GAP = no statement found at grade A or B for that company (C-grade posts were not used to fill gaps). "
                "'Shared' = statements about both companies.")
stance_counts = pd.crosstab([s4_statements["company"], s4_statements["speaker_type"]], s4_statements["stance"])
stance_counts.columns.name = None
show_table(stance_counts.reset_index(), "Stance by speaker type and company")


claims = pd.read_csv(DATA_DIR / "claims.csv").merge(
    s4_statements[["statement_id", "speaker", "date", "grade", "source_id"]], on="statement_id", how="left", validate="many_to_one")
assert claims["speaker"].notna().all(), "claim points to a missing statement"


def nearest_booked(company, month):
    # Booked period whose middle month is closest to `month` (within 6 months), annualised.
    m = pd.Period(month, freq="M")
    d = revenue_model[(revenue_model["company"] == company) & revenue_model["type"].isin(BOOKED_MONTHS)].copy()
    if d.empty:
        return None
    d["n"] = d["type"].map(BOOKED_MONTHS)
    d["gap"] = [abs((pd.Period(p, freq="M") - m).n - (n - 1) / 2) for p, n in zip(d["period"], d["n"])]
    d = d[d["gap"] <= 6].sort_values(["gap", "n"])
    if d.empty:
        return None
    r = d.iloc[0]
    return r["value"] * 12 / r["n"], f"{REVENUE_TYPES[r['type']].split(', ')[1]} to {r['period']} annualised"


def ratio_verdict(ratio, ok=(0.85, 1e9), near=(0.6, 1e9)):
    return "supported" if ok[0] <= ratio <= ok[1] else "partly" if near[0] <= ratio <= near[1] else "not supported"


def check_claim(c):
    # One function for both companies: compares a claim with values from Sections 1-3. Returns (model says, verdict).
    co = c["company"]
    if c["check_type"] == "run_rate":
        b = nearest_booked(co, c["period"])
        if b is None:
            return "No booked revenue near that date", "can't check yet: GAP"
        return f"Booked revenue ({b[1]}): ${b[0]:.1f}B", ratio_verdict(b[0] / c["claimed_value"])
    if c["check_type"] in ("growth_multiple", "annualised_growth"):
        path = monthly_run_rate_path(co)
        start, end = pd.Period(c["period_start"], freq="M"), pd.Period(c["period"], freq="M")
        model = path.loc[end] / path.loc[start]
        if c["check_type"] == "annualised_growth":
            model = model ** (12 / (end - start).n)
            claimed = c["claimed_value"]
        else:
            claimed = c["claimed_value"] / c["baseline_value"]
        ratio = model / claimed
        verdict = "supported" if 0.8 <= ratio <= 1.25 else "partly" if 0.2 <= ratio <= 5 else "not supported"
        return f"Run-rate path {start.strftime('%b %Y')}-{end.strftime('%b %Y')}: {model:.1f}x (claim {claimed:.1f}x)", verdict
    if c["check_type"] == "losses_continue":
        ue = s3_unit_economics.set_index(["company", "period"]).loc[(co, "FY2025")]
        burn = "GAP" if pd.isna(ue["cash_burn"]) else f"${ue['cash_burn']:.1f}B"
        verdict = "supported" if ue["operating_loss"] > 0 else "not supported"
        return f"FY2025 operating loss ${ue['operating_loss']:.1f}B ({pct(ue['operating_margin'], 0)} margin); cash burn {burn}", verdict
    if c["check_type"] == "profit_projection":
        ue = s3_unit_economics.set_index(["company", "period"]).loc[(co, "FY2025")]
        return (f"A projection for {c['claimed_value']:.0f}; latest actual FY2025 operating margin {pct(ue['operating_margin'], 0)}",
                "can't check yet: GAP")
    if c["check_type"] == "commitment_vs_plan":
        ref = financials[(financials["company"] == co) & (financials["source_id"] != c["source_id"])
                         & financials["metric"].isin(["future_compute_commitments", "compute_and_infrastructure_spend_through_2030"])]
        if ref.empty:
            return "No independent figure", "can't check yet: GAP"
        r = ref.sort_values("date_published").iloc[-1]
        verdict = "supported" if c["claimed_value"] <= r["value"] else ratio_verdict(r["value"] / c["claimed_value"], near=(0.5, 1e9))
        return f"{r['metric'].replace('_', ' ')}: ${r['value']:,.0f}B ({r['source_id']}, {r['period']})", verdict
    if c["check_type"] == "valuation":
        paid = multiples[(multiples["company"] == co) & multiples["type"].isin(CLOSED_TYPES)]["x_run_rate"]
        x = c["claimed_value"] / latest_rr[co]["value"]
        verdict = "supported" if x <= paid.max() else "not supported"
        return f"{x:.0f}x latest run-rate vs {paid.min():.0f}-{paid.max():.0f}x paid in past rounds", verdict
    raise ValueError(c["check_type"])


checked = claims.apply(lambda c: pd.Series(check_claim(c), index=["what my model says", "verdict"]), axis=1)
s4_claim_checks = pd.concat([claims, checked], axis=1)
assert s4_claim_checks["verdict"].isin(VERDICTS).all()
show_table(s4_claim_checks.assign(date=s4_claim_checks["date"].dt.date)[
    ["claim_id", "company", "claim", "check_type", "speaker", "date", "grade", "source_id", "what my model says", "verdict", "notes"]],
    "Claim checks, full detail (s4_claim_checks)")


bull_bear_raw = pd.read_csv(DATA_DIR / "bull_bear.csv").merge(source_log[["source_id", "grade"]], on="source_id", how="left", validate="many_to_one")
assert bull_bear_raw["grade"].notna().all()


def evidence(company, key):
    # A short evidence line built from Section 1-3 outputs (no re-typed numbers).
    ue = s3_unit_economics.set_index(["company", "period"]).loc[(company, "FY2025")]
    rr = latest_rr[company]
    if key == "booked_and_run_rate":
        return f"FY2025 booked ${ue['revenue_usd_bn']:.1f}B; latest run-rate ${rr['value']:g}B ({rr['period_end']:%b %Y})"
    if key == "capital_raised":
        return f"${funding.loc[funding['company'] == company, 'amount_counted_usd_bn'].sum():.0f}B counted since 2023"
    if key == "burn_multiple":
        return f"Burn multiple {burn.set_index('company').loc[company, 'burn multiple (cash / new ARR)']:.2f}x in 2025"
    if key == "commit_years":
        return f"Commitments = {capital_needs(company)['commitments / latest run-rate (years of revenue)']:.0f} years of current run-rate"
    if key == "funding_gap":
        return f"Gap on own projections: ${gaps3.set_index('company').loc[company, 'gap on own projections (USD bn)']:.0f}B"
    if key == "q2_check":
        q = q_check.query("company == @company").iloc[-1]
        return f"{q['quarter']} revenue x4 = ${q['quarter revenue x4 (USD bn)']:g}B; run-rates in quarter: {q['reported run-rates in the quarter']}"
    if key == "top_customers":
        t = financials.query("company == @company and metric == 'top2_customer_revenue_share'")
        return "GAP" if t.empty else f"Two customers ~{t.iloc[0]['value']:g}% of 2025 revenue"
    if key == "op_margin":
        return f"FY2025 operating margin {pct(ue['operating_margin'], 0)}; commitments ${capital_needs(company)['compute commitments (USD bn)']:,.0f}B"
    return "-"


bull_bear = bull_bear_raw.assign(evidence=[evidence(c, k) for c, k in zip(bull_bear_raw["company"], bull_bear_raw["evidence_key"])])
assert (bull_bear.groupby(["company", "side"]).size() == 3).all(), "3 bull and 3 bear arguments per company"


def risk_flags(company):
    # Up to 3 descriptive risk flags for Section 5, from data already in the model (no weights).
    flags = []
    top = financials.query("company == @company and metric == 'top2_customer_revenue_share'")
    if not top.empty:
        flags.append(f"Customer concentration (two customers ~{top.iloc[0]['value']:g}% of revenue)")
    if (funding[funding["company"] == company]["type"] == "strategic").any():
        flags.append("Circular funding: suppliers are also investors")
    if (s4_statements.query("company == @company and speaker_type == 'regulator'")["stance"] == "bearish").any():
        flags.append("Regulatory / political action against the company")
    if capital_needs(company)["commitments / latest run-rate (years of revenue)"] > 10:
        flags.append("Compute commitments above 10 years of current revenue")
    if gaps3.set_index("company").loc[company, "gap on own projections (USD bn)"] > 0:
        flags.append("Needs new capital even on its own projections")
    gm = financials.query("company == @company and metric in ['gross_margin_fy', 'adjusted_gross_margin_fy'] and period == '2025-12'")
    actual, proj = gm[gm["figure_type"].isin(["reported", "adjusted"])], gm[gm["figure_type"] == "projection"].sort_values("date_published")
    if (not actual.empty and not proj.empty and actual["value"].iloc[0] < proj["value"].max()) or (len(proj) > 1 and proj["value"].iloc[-1] < proj["value"].iloc[0]):
        flags.append("Missed or cut its own gross-margin forecast")
    return flags[:3]


def signals(company):
    rows = s4_statements[s4_statements["company"].isin([company, "Both"])]
    v = s4_claim_checks[s4_claim_checks["company"] == company]["verdict"].value_counts()
    out = {"statements (incl. shared)": len(rows)}
    out.update({f"stance: {s}": int((rows["stance"] == s).sum()) for s in STANCES})
    out.update({f"verdict: {x}": int(v.get(x, 0)) for x in VERDICTS})
    flags = risk_flags(company)
    out.update({f"risk flag {i + 1}": flags[i] if i < len(flags) else "-" for i in range(3)})
    return pd.Series(out, name=company)


s4_signals = pd.concat([signals(c) for c in COMPANIES], axis=1)
show_table(s4_signals.reset_index(names="signal"), "Signals for Section 5 (s4_signals): counts and risk flags",
           note="Descriptive only: no weights or probabilities. Shared statements count for both companies.")


def claim_table():
    return s4_claim_checks.assign(date=s4_claim_checks["date"].dt.strftime("%b %Y"), who=s4_claim_checks["speaker"])[
        ["company", "claim", "who", "date", "grade", "what my model says", "verdict"]]

4.1 Who's talking, and what do they want?¶

Everyone who comments on these companies has a reason to say what they say. Executives and investors are "talking their book": they gain if people believe the good news. Before an IPO this gets stronger, because a higher listing price makes existing shareholders richer. Critics and rivals have their own angles too. So I weigh each statement by who said it, and check the numbers against my own data.

Speaker type What they usually want How much weight I give it
Executive A higher valuation, happy staff, more funding Low for opinions; medium for figures they put their name to
Investor Their stake to look good; often also a supplier Low: they are rarely neutral
Analyst To be right and to be noticed Medium
Critic To be proven right; attention Medium: useful for spotting risks
Competitor To make the rival look worse Low: grade C, sensitivity only
Regulator Rules followed, markets kept open High for facts, but slow and political

4.2 Claims vs my numbers¶

I took the six biggest public claims for each company and checked each against my numbers from Sections 1–3, using the same function for both. Verdicts:

  • supported: my numbers agree;
  • partly: right direction but a different size;
  • not supported: my numbers disagree;
  • can't check yet: GAP: no data yet, usually because the claim is about the future.

For valuation claims, "supported" only means the price is in line with what investors have already paid. It does not mean it is a fair price.

4.3 The bull and bear case¶

The three strongest arguments on each side for each company, with their source and grade. The evidence column is built from my Sections 1–3 outputs, not re-typed.

Anthropic bear Revenue is concentrated in a few large customers, many without long-term contracts. Two customers ~25% of 2025 revenue AN13 B
Anthropic bear Still deeply loss-making at the operating level, with very large compute commitments. FY2025 operating margin -175%; commitments $518B AN11 B
Anthropic bear Political risk: the Pentagon has designated it a supply-chain risk. - AN29 B

My judgement (not a sourced fact): on growth, the evidence leans bull for both, because booked revenue backs up the run-rate claims. On financial risk it leans bear for OpenAI (compute commitments worth decades of its current revenue, and a funding gap even on its own plan). For Anthropic it is mixed: it can fund itself on its own projections, but its customers are concentrated and it is in a dispute with the Pentagon.

Key Takeaways¶

  • There are multiple stakeholders, each their their motive. Their statements can influence the companies.
  • Most claims are supported by the revenue figures. However, certain claims can be misleading where they are constantly revised.
  • Both bullish and bearish claims can be justifiably made for both companies however there is an overarching bullish sentiment to Anthropic and OpenAI.

5. Scenarios¶

The question: Nobody knows how this ends, so what are the realistic futures for each company, and how likely is each one?

▶ Show code
# Setup for Section 5: company projections, scenario assumptions and the four futures (no output here).
# Detail tables produced here are captured and shown, collapsed, in Appendix A5. No valuation is computed yet.
capture_to("A5")

SCENARIOS = ["Bust", "Bear", "Base", "Bull"]
SCENARIO_STORIES = {  # identical for both companies
    "Bust": "Fails to stay independent or is sold cheaply (cash runs out / falls behind)",
    "Bear": "Survives, but growth fades fast and margins stay thin",
    "Base": "Growth slows steadily, becomes solidly profitable",
    "Bull": "Stays a top-2 AI lab, very large and profitable",
}
DRIVERS = ["growth_2027", "growth_2030", "op_margin_2030", "extra_capital_needed"]
PROJECTION_METRICS = ["revenue", "operating_margin", "cash_burn", "profit_turn_year", "capex_compute"]
ANCHORS = ["projection", "my Sections 1-3", "assumption"]
YEARS = [2026, 2027, 2028, 2029, 2030]

# --- The companies' own forward numbers (projections.csv) ---
projections_s5 = pd.read_csv(DATA_DIR / "projections.csv").merge(
    source_log[["source_id", "date_published", "grade"]], on="source_id", how="left", validate="many_to_one")
assert projections_s5["metric"].isin(PROJECTION_METRICS).all(), f"metric must be one of {PROJECTION_METRICS}"
is_gap = projections_s5["source_id"] == "GAP"
assert projections_s5.loc[is_gap, "value"].isna().all() and projections_s5.loc[~is_gap, "value"].notna().all(), "GAP rows have no value"
assert projections_s5.loc[~is_gap, "grade"].isin(["A", "B"]).all(), "projections must come from A/B sources"
assert set(projections_s5.query("metric == 'revenue'")["company"]) == set(COMPANIES)
projections_s5["grade"] = projections_s5["grade"].fillna("GAP")

# Consistency: a projection already stored upstream must carry the same value here (no silent re-typing).
for r in projections_s5.query("metric == 'revenue' and source_id != 'GAP'").itertuples():
    up = revenue_model[(revenue_model["company"] == r.company) & (revenue_model["source_id"] == r.source_id)
                       & (revenue_model["type"] == "projection") & (revenue_model["period"] == f"{r.year}-12")]
    assert up.empty or np.isclose(up["value"].iloc[0], r.value), f"projections.csv disagrees with revenue.csv: {r}"


def own_forecasts(company, metric):
    # The company's own forecasts for one metric, latest source per year (by publication date).
    d = projections_s5[(projections_s5["company"] == company) & (projections_s5["metric"] == metric) & (projections_s5["source_id"] != "GAP")]
    return d.sort_values("date_published").groupby("year").tail(1).sort_values("year")


# --- Comparable basis: the gross-vs-net adjustment from 2.2 (Axios high end, grade B) ---
NET_HAIRCUT = ev.loc["net_switch_haircut_high", "value"] / 100
REPORTING_BASIS = {c: revenue_model.query("company == @c and type == 'run_rate'").sort_values("period_end")["revenue_basis"].iloc[-1]
                   for c in COMPANIES}


def to_net(company, value):
    # Put a figure on the comparable (net) basis: gross reporters lose NET_HAIRCUT, net reporters are unchanged.
    # Projections with an 'unknown' basis are assumed to follow the company's own reporting basis.
    return value * (1 - NET_HAIRCUT) if REPORTING_BASIS[company] == "gross" else value


def fy2026_start(company):
    # FY2026 revenue if the run-rate never grows again after its latest month: bridge estimate so far + latest run-rate
    # for the remaining months (the 'zero-growth floor' from 2.3). Net basis. A conservative starting point.
    rr = latest_rr[company]
    n = rr["period_end"].month
    gross_or_net = estimate_booked_revenue(company, rr["period"], n) + (12 - n) * rr["value"] / 12
    return to_net(company, gross_or_net)


# --- Scenario assumptions (judgement calls, each anchored) ---
assumptions = pd.read_csv(DATA_DIR / "scenario_assumptions.csv")
assert assumptions["anchor"].isin(ANCHORS).all(), f"anchor must be one of {ANCHORS}"
assert assumptions["scenario"].isin(SCENARIOS).all()
cited = assumptions.loc[assumptions["source_id"] != "own", "source_id"]
assert cited.isin(source_log["source_id"]).all(), "assumption cites an unknown source_id"
for c in COMPANIES:  # symmetry: every company has every driver in every scenario
    got = assumptions[assumptions["company"] == c].set_index(["scenario", "driver"]).index
    assert set(got) == {(s, d) for s in SCENARIOS for d in DRIVERS}, f"{c}: missing or extra assumptions"
BUST_VALUE_MULTIPLE = assumptions.query("company == 'Both' and driver == 'bust_value_multiple'")["value"].iloc[0]


def assumption(company, scenario, driver):
    return assumptions.query("company == @company and scenario == @scenario and driver == @driver")["value"].iloc[0]


def growth_path(g2027, g2030):
    # Annual growth for 2027-2030, fading in a straight line from g2027 to g2030 (Section 6 uses the same rule).
    return {y: g2027 + (g2030 - g2027) * (y - 2027) / 3 for y in YEARS[1:]}


def revenue_path(start, g2027, g2030):
    # FY revenue 2026-2030 (USD bn, net basis) from the FY2026 start and the growth fade.
    path, rev = {2026: start}, start
    for y, g in growth_path(g2027, g2030).items():
        rev *= 1 + g
        path[y] = rev
    return path


def build_scenarios(company):
    # The four futures for one company: same function, same drivers for both companies (symmetry rule).
    start = fy2026_start(company)
    rows = []
    for s in SCENARIOS:
        g27, g30 = assumption(company, s, "growth_2027"), assumption(company, s, "growth_2030")
        path = revenue_path(start, g27, g30)
        rows.append({"company": company, "scenario": s, "story": SCENARIO_STORIES[s], "fy2026_start_net": start,
                     **{f"revenue_{y}": path[y] for y in YEARS[1:]},
                     "growth_2027": g27, "growth_2030": g30,
                     "op_margin_2030": assumption(company, s, "op_margin_2030"),
                     "extra_capital_needed": assumption(company, s, "extra_capital_needed"),
                     "bust_value_multiple": BUST_VALUE_MULTIPLE if s == "Bust" else np.nan})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


scenario_drivers = pd.concat([build_scenarios(c) for c in COMPANIES], ignore_index=True)
assert (scenario_drivers.groupby("company")["revenue_2030"].apply(lambda r: r.is_monotonic_increasing)).all(), \
    "revenue_2030 must rise from Bust to Bull"


# --- Anchors from Sections 1-4, shown next to each judgement (computed, never re-typed) ---
def anchor_value(company, driver):
    rr = latest_rr[company]
    ue = s3_unit_economics.set_index(["company", "period"]).loc[(company, "FY2025")]
    g = gaps3.set_index("company").loc[company]
    if driver == "growth_2027":
        lift = to_net(company, rr["value"]) / fy2026_start(company) - 1
        return (f"Latest run-rate is {pct(lift, 0)} above the FY2026 start, so FY2027 grows that much with no further growth; "
                f"run-rate growth now {pct(s2_growth.loc['latest_interval_annualised', company], 0)}/yr (2.1)")
    if driver == "growth_2030":
        return "No data: a judgement about maturity"
    if driver == "op_margin_2030":
        own = own_forecasts(company, "operating_margin")
        own_txt = "; ".join(f"own {r.year}: {pct(r.value, 0)} ({r.source_id})" for r in own.itertuples()) or "own forecast: GAP"
        return f"FY2025 actual {pct(ue['operating_margin'], 0)} (3.2); {own_txt}"
    if driver == "extra_capital_needed":
        return (f"Gap on own plan ${g['gap on own projections (USD bn)']:.0f}B; cash available "
                f"{'>= ' if g['cash available is a lower bound'] else ''}${g['cash available (USD bn)']:.0f}B; "
                f"commitments {capital_needs(company)['commitments / latest run-rate (years of revenue)']:.0f} years of revenue (3.3)")
    return "-"


reasoning = assumptions.assign(
    from_my_model=[anchor_value(c, d) if c in COMPANIES else "-" for c, d in zip(assumptions["company"], assumptions["driver"])])

show_table(projections_s5[["company", "year", "metric", "value", "unit", "basis", "grade", "source_id", "note"]]
           .sort_values(["company", "metric", "year"]),
           "The companies' own forward numbers (projections.csv)",
           note="Latest forecast per year is used; older ones stay for history. GAP = not found in an A/B source "
                "(weaker sources are not used to fill it). Revenue forecasts also in revenue.csv are checked to match it.")
show_table(reasoning[["company", "scenario", "driver", "value", "anchor", "source_id", "why", "from_my_model"]],
           "Every scenario assumption and the reasoning behind it (scenario_assumptions.csv)",
           note="value = my judgement. from_my_model = the Section 1-3 numbers I looked at, computed here, not re-typed. "
                "Growth and margins are fractions; capital in USD bn.")
show_table(scenario_drivers[["company", "scenario", "fy2026_start_net"] + [f"revenue_{y}" for y in YEARS[1:]]].round(1),
           "Revenue paths implied by each scenario (USD bn, net basis)",
           note=f"FY2026 start = revenue booked so far (bridge estimate) + latest run-rate for the remaining months, i.e. no "
                f"further growth. Anthropic is cut by {pct(NET_HAIRCUT, 0)} to a net basis (2.2). Growth fades in a straight line "
                "from 2027 to 2030.")


def base_check(company):
    # Base revenue vs the company's own forecast for the same year (both net basis). Explain any year where Base is above.
    base = scenario_drivers.query("company == @company and scenario == 'Base'").iloc[0]
    own = own_forecasts(company, "revenue")
    rows = []
    for r in own[own["year"] >= 2027].itertuples():
        mine, theirs = base[f"revenue_{r.year}"], to_net(company, r.value)
        if mine <= theirs:
            why = "-"
        else:
            newer_higher = own[(own["date_published"] > r.date_published) & (own["value"] > r.value)]
            overtaken = to_net(company, latest_rr[company]["value"]) >= theirs
            why = "; ".join(filter(None, [
                f"stale: its newer forecast for an earlier year is already higher "
                f"({', '.join(f'FY{x.year} ${x.value:g}B, {x.source_id}' for x in newer_higher.itertuples())})"
                if not newer_higher.empty else "",
                "today's run-rate is already above it" if overtaken else ""])) or "NO REASON FOUND: review"
        rows.append({"company": company, "year": r.year, "own forecast (net basis)": theirs, "source": f"{r.source_id} ({r.grade})",
                     "my Base (net basis)": mine, "Base vs own": "below" if mine <= theirs else "ABOVE", "why": why})
    if not (own["year"] == 2030).any():
        rows.append({"company": company, "year": 2030, "own forecast (net basis)": np.nan, "source": "GAP",
                     "my Base (net basis)": base["revenue_2030"], "Base vs own": "no own forecast", "why": "-"})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


s5_base_check = pd.concat([base_check(c) for c in COMPANIES], ignore_index=True)
assert not (s5_base_check["why"] == "NO REASON FOUND: review").any(), "a Base year is above management's number without a reason"
show_table(s5_base_check.round(1), "Base vs each company's own revenue forecast",
           note="Base may not sit above management's number without a stated reason. Bull may exceed it. "
                "Projections with an unknown basis are put on the company's own reporting basis, then made net.")


def plot_scenario_revenue():
    # revenue_2030 by scenario for both companies, with today's run-rate (net basis) marked for reference.
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5))
    x = np.arange(len(SCENARIOS))
    for i, company in enumerate(COMPANIES):
        d = scenario_drivers[scenario_drivers["company"] == company].set_index("scenario").loc[SCENARIOS]
        xs = x + (i - 0.5) * 0.22
        colour = COMPANY_COLOURS[company]
        ax.scatter(xs, d["revenue_2030"], s=90, color=colour, zorder=3, label=f"{company}: FY2030 revenue")
        for xi, v in zip(xs, d["revenue_2030"]):
            ax.annotate(f"${v:,.0f}B", (xi, v), textcoords="offset points", xytext=(0, 8), ha="center", fontsize=8.5, color=colour)
        rr = latest_rr[company]
        ax.axhline(to_net(company, rr["value"]), color=colour, lw=1.2, ls="--", zorder=1,
                   label=f"{company}: today's run-rate, net (${to_net(company, rr['value']):.0f}B, {rr['period_end']:%b %Y})")
    ax.set_xticks(x, SCENARIOS)
    ax.set_ylabel("FY2030 revenue (USD bn, net basis)")
    ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: f"${v:,.0f}B"))
    ax.set_ylim(0, scenario_drivers["revenue_2030"].max() * 1.15)
    ax.set_title("FY2030 revenue in each future (judgement, not a forecast)", loc="left", fontsize=12)
    ax.grid(True, axis="y", color="#dddddd", lw=0.7)
    ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
    ax.legend(loc="upper left", fontsize=8.5, frameon=False)
    fig.text(0.01, -0.02, f"Net basis: Anthropic's figures are cut by {pct(NET_HAIRCUT, 0)} (2.2). Dashed lines = latest reported "
             "run-rate, for scale only.", fontsize=8.5, color="#444444", va="top")
    plt.tight_layout()
    return fig


def drivers_table():
    # The four drivers for every company x scenario, formatted for reading.
    d = scenario_drivers
    capital = [f"${v:,.0f}B" + (" (not raised)" if s == "Bust" else "") for v, s in zip(d["extra_capital_needed"], d["scenario"])]
    return pd.DataFrame({"company": d["company"], "scenario": d["scenario"],
                         "revenue 2030 (net)": d["revenue_2030"].map(lambda v: f"${v:,.0f}B"),
                         "growth 2027": d["growth_2027"].map(lambda v: pct(v, 0)), "growth 2030": d["growth_2030"].map(lambda v: pct(v, 0)),
                         "operating margin 2030": d["op_margin_2030"].map(lambda v: pct(v, 0)),
                         "extra capital to 2030": capital})


reference = pd.read_csv(DATA_DIR / "reference_figures.csv").merge(source_log[["source_id", "grade"]], on="source_id", how="left")
assert reference["grade"].notna().all(), "reference figure with no matching source"


def sense_check_line():
    # One sentence: Bull FY2030 revenue vs Microsoft's latest full-year revenue.
    ms = reference.query("item == 'Microsoft revenue'").iloc[0]
    bull = scenario_drivers.query("scenario == 'Bull'").set_index("company")["revenue_2030"]
    ratio = bull / ms["value"]
    parts = " and ".join(f"{c} ${bull[c]:,.0f}B ({ratio[c]:.1f}x Microsoft)" for c in COMPANIES)
    size = "bigger than" if ratio.min() > 1.05 else "about as big as" if ratio.min() > 0.9 else "a large fraction of"
    text = (f"**Sense-check:** Bull's FY2030 revenue is {parts}, against Microsoft's ${ms['value']:g}B in {ms['period']} "
            f"({ms['source_id']}, grade {ms['grade']}). So Bull means becoming {size} Microsoft is today, within four years.")
    return text.replace("$", "\\$")  # escaped so Jupyter doesn't read $...$ as maths


def base_check_line():
    # One sentence per company on Base vs management's own revenue forecast.
    out = []
    for c in COMPANIES:
        d = s5_base_check[s5_base_check["company"] == c]
        own = own_forecasts(c, "revenue")
        newest = own[own["year"] >= 2027].sort_values("date_published").iloc[-1]  # the company's most recent forecast
        row = d[d["year"] == newest["year"]].iloc[0]
        txt = (f"- **{c}:** Base FY{row['year']} ${row['my Base (net basis)']:,.0f}B vs its newest own forecast "
               f"${row['own forecast (net basis)']:,.0f}B ({row['source']}, net basis): **{row['Base vs own']}**.")
        above = d[d["Base vs own"] == "ABOVE"]
        if not above.empty:
            txt += (" Base is above its older forecasts for " + " and ".join(f"FY{y}" for y in above["year"])
                    + " because they are " + above["why"].iloc[0].split(";")[0] + ".")
        out.append(txt)
    return "\n".join(out).replace("$", "\\$")  # escaped so Jupyter doesn't read $...$ as maths


# --- Probabilities: evidence and outputs (the numbers themselves live in SCENARIO_PROBS, in 5.3) ---
def evidence_lines():
    # One evidence line per scenario, built from Sections 1-4 outputs (s4_signals risk flags included).
    order = ["Anthropic", "OpenAI"]  # same order as the probability columns
    fy25 = s3_unit_economics.set_index(["company", "period"]).xs("FY2025", level="period")
    years = {c: f"{capital_needs(c)['commitments / latest run-rate (years of revenue)']:.0f}" for c in order}
    gap = {c: f"${gaps3.set_index('company').loc[c, 'gap on own projections (USD bn)']:.0f}B" for c in order}
    flags = {c: "; ".join(f for f in s4_signals.loc[s4_signals.index.str.startswith("risk flag"), c] if f != "-") for c in order}
    growth_now = {c: pct(s2_growth.loc["latest_interval_cmgr", c]) + "/month" for c in order}
    supported = {c: f"{s4_signals.loc['verdict: supported', c]} supported" for c in order}
    booked = {c: f"${fy25.loc[c, 'revenue_usd_bn']:.1f}B" for c in order}
    profit_year = {c: f"{own_forecasts(c, 'profit_turn_year')['value'].min():.0f}" for c in order}
    margin = {c: pct(fy25.loc[c, "operating_margin"], 0) for c in order}
    both = lambda d: " / ".join(f"{c} {d[c]}" for c in order)
    return {
        "Bust": f"Compute commitments in years of current revenue: {both(years)}; gap on own plan: {both(gap)} (3.3)",
        "Bear": f"Section 4 risk flags: {both(flags)}. Growth now: {both(growth_now)}; OpenAI slowing (2.3)",
        "Base": f"Revenue claims checked: {both(supported)} (4.2); FY2025 booked revenue: {both(booked)} (1.2)",
        "Bull": f"Own profit year: {both(profit_year)}; FY2025 operating margin: {both(margin)} (3.2)",
    }


def finalise_scenarios(probs):
    # s5_probs (scenario x company) and s5_scenarios (one row per company x scenario: drivers + probability).
    for c in COMPANIES:
        assert set(probs[c]) == set(SCENARIOS), f"{c}: probabilities must cover {SCENARIOS}"
        assert all(0 <= p <= 1 for p in probs[c].values()), f"{c}: probabilities must be between 0 and 1"
        assert np.isclose(sum(probs[c].values()), 1), f"{c}: probabilities must sum to 1"
    p = pd.DataFrame(probs).loc[SCENARIOS, COMPANIES]
    p.index.name = "scenario"
    s = scenario_drivers.assign(probability=[probs[c][sc] for c, sc in zip(scenario_drivers["company"], scenario_drivers["scenario"])])
    cols = ["company", "scenario", "story", "fy2026_start_net", "revenue_2030", "growth_2027", "growth_2030",
            "op_margin_2030", "extra_capital_needed", "bust_value_multiple", "probability"] + [f"revenue_{y}" for y in YEARS[1:-1]]
    return p, s[cols].reset_index(drop=True)


def probability_table(probs):
    ev_lines = evidence_lines()
    return pd.DataFrame([{"scenario": s, "Anthropic prob": pct(probs["Anthropic"][s], 0), "OpenAI prob": pct(probs["OpenAI"][s], 0),
                          "evidence that moved it": ev_lines[s]} for s in SCENARIOS])


def bull_whatif_table(probs, step=0.10):
    # Move each company's Bull probability by +/- step, taken evenly from (or given evenly to) the other three.
    rows = []
    for c in COMPANIES:
        rev = scenario_drivers[scenario_drivers["company"] == c].set_index("scenario")["revenue_2030"]
        for delta in [-step, 0.0, step]:
            p = {s: probs[c][s] - delta / 3 if s != "Bull" else probs[c][s] + delta for s in SCENARIOS}
            ok = all(v >= 0 for v in p.values())
            rows.append({"company": c, "Bull probability": pct(p["Bull"], 0), "change": f"{delta * 100:+.0f} pts",
                         "others each": f"{-delta / 3 * 100:+.1f} pts",
                         "expected FY2030 revenue (USD bn, net)": sum(p[s] * rev[s] for s in SCENARIOS) if ok else np.nan})
    out = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    base = out[out["change"] == "+0 pts"].set_index("company")["expected FY2030 revenue (USD bn, net)"]
    out["vs draft"] = [pct(v / base[c] - 1) for c, v in zip(out["company"], out["expected FY2030 revenue (USD bn, net)"])]
    return out.round(1)


capture_to(None)

5.1 Why scenarios, not one forecast¶

One forecast gives one number and hides how unsure it is. For a young company the possible outcomes are spread very wide, from being sold cheaply to becoming one of the biggest companies in the world.

Venture investors think in outcomes and probabilities: list a few futures, give each a chance, and accept that most of the value can sit in the one good outcome.

So I use four futures with the same names and stories for both companies. Only the numbers behind them differ, and each number is anchored to something in Sections 1–4.

▶ Show code

           "The four futures (identical for both companies)", collapsed=False)
▶ Show table: The four futures (identical for both companies) (4 rows)
scenario story
Bust Fails to stay independent or is sold cheaply (cash runs out / falls behind)
Bear Survives, but growth fades fast and margins stay thin
Base Growth slows steadily, becomes solidly profitable
Bull Stays a top-2 AI lab, very large and profitable

5.2 What each future assumes¶

Each future has four drivers (the inputs that shape the forecast):

  • Revenue in 2030. Computed, not picked: FY2026 revenue (if growth stopped today) grown along the path below.
  • Growth fade: annual growth in 2027 and in 2030, falling in a straight line in between.
  • Operating margin in 2030: operating profit ÷ revenue.
  • Extra capital needed from now to 2030. In Bust, it is money the company fails to raise; a buyer then pays about 1× revenue (my assumption, grade C).

All revenue is on one net basis: Anthropic's figures are cut by the same 10% used in 2.2. OpenAI's are already net.

5.3 How likely is each?¶

These probabilities are my judgement, not data. The evidence in the table moved them, but no formula turns evidence into a number. They sit in one small code cell so I can change them.

Sections 7–9 will show how much the valuation depends on them. Appendix A5 already shows that moving Bull by 10 points shifts expected 2030 revenue by more than a tenth.

Key Takeaways¶

  • Four different scenarios indicating different levels of growth; bust, bear, base, bull.
  • Bullish growth for both companies means that they will become larger than Microsoft in terms of 2030 revenue.
  • Revenue forecasts are constantly changing, as indicated through the old and new change in Anthropic's forecast for FY 2028 compared to my Base forecast for the same year.
  • Both companies have the highest probability of the Base scenario for FY 2030 as per me. There are certain constrictions that makes bullish growth a lower possibility but the optimism around the industry also limits the probability for the Bust scenario.

6. Forecasts: from revenue to cash¶

The question: if each scenario comes true, how much cash would these companies actually produce, and when?

The model's adjustable inputs sit in one control panel (the first code cell below, ASSUMPTIONS), next to the probabilities in 5.3.

▶ Show code
# ===================== CONTROL PANEL – edit me =====================
# Every model assumption lives here or in SCENARIO_PROBS (5.3). Section 7 adds its own entries to this dict.
ASSUMPTIONS = {
    "LONG_RUN_GROWTH": 0.04,    # DRAFT, grade C (my judgement): revenue growth reached by FORECAST_END and kept after it
    "TAX_RATE": 0.21,           # grade A: US federal corporate rate, 26 U.S.C. 11(b) (BX9); ignores state tax and credits
    "SALES_TO_CAPITAL": 3.0,    # DRAFT, grade C: $ of new revenue per $1 invested in what the company BUILDS OR OWNS.
                                #   The labs mostly rent compute (cloud deals, 3.3), and that rent is already inside operating
                                #   costs (the margin), so counting it here again would charge it twice. Owned assets are a
                                #   thin layer (offices, some chips and data centres), so each $1 supports more revenue than at
                                #   a software firm that owns its servers. Damodaran Jan 2026 (BX8): software 1.35-1.54,
                                #   semiconductors 1.21 (whole capital base, owned + rented); 3.0 = about 2x software. Was 1.0.
    "BUST_YEAR": 2028,          # DRAFT, grade C (my judgement): the year a Bust company is sold
    "BUST_VALUE_MULTIPLE": float(s5_scenarios.query("scenario == 'Bust'")["bust_value_multiple"].unique().item()),
                                # grade C: read from Section 5 (scenario_assumptions.csv), not re-typed
    "FORECAST_END": 2035,       # model choice: ten fiscal years, FY2026-FY2035
    # --- Section 7: turning future cash into today's value ---
    "BASE_COST_OF_CAPITAL": 0.10,  # grade C: Damodaran Jan 2026 (BX10) cost of capital, software 9.3%, internet software 10.7%,
                                   #   semiconductors 10.6%; rounded to 10% for a large public tech company
    "PRIVATE_PREMIUM": 0.04,       # DRAFT, grade C (my judgement): extra return for shares that are pre-IPO and hard to sell.
                                   #   Illiquidity only, NOT failure risk: failure is the Bust probability in 5.3
    "IPO_YEAR": 2027,              # DRAFT, grade C (my judgement): the premium is paid in full up to and including this year
                                   #   (both filed S-1s confidentially in June 2026)
    "PREMIUM_FADE_END": 2030,      # DRAFT, grade C (my judgement): after the IPO the premium fades in a straight line and is
                                   #   gone by this year; from then on the rate is BASE_COST_OF_CAPITAL (also used for the terminal value)
    "SCENARIO_VALUE_FLOOR": 0.0,   # DRAFT, grade C (my judgement): no future is worth less than this. Owners can lose what they
                                   #   put in, no more (limited liability); on a value-destroying path they would stop funding or sell
    "TV_FLOOR_AT_ZERO": True,      # DRAFT, grade C (my judgement): a business still losing cash in 2035 is worth 0 after it,
                                   #   not minus forever (owners would stop funding it)
    "EXIT_EV_SALES": float(reference.set_index("item").loc["EV/Sales: Software (System & Application)", "value"]),
                                   # grade C: Damodaran Jan 2026 (BX11), read from reference_figures.csv; cross-check only (A7)
    "VALUATION_DATE": "2026-10-06",  # today (the day Section 7 was built); move it forward when re-valuing
}
# Derived from the entries above: change those, not these.
ASSUMPTIONS["DISCOUNT_RATE"] = ASSUMPTIONS["BASE_COST_OF_CAPITAL"] + ASSUMPTIONS["PRIVATE_PREMIUM"]  # the 2026 rate (display); same for both
ASSUMPTIONS["TERMINAL_GROWTH"] = ASSUMPTIONS["LONG_RUN_GROWTH"]  # growth after FORECAST_END = the rate the forecast fades to
